AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has named his starting line-up for the Sunday evening San Siro clash with Frosinone.

Milan went into the international break inside the top four, but Como’s win on Saturday has pushed them back out, so there is some added pressure tonight. It will not be an easy game against a newly-promoted Frosinone side who have started the season very well and are full of confidence.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Strahinja Pavlovic is back in the matchday squad after a kidney issue sidelined him, but Amorim has chosen not to risk him from minute one. A back four of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Davide Bartesaghi will operate in front of Mike Maignan.

It looks like Luka Modric will be flanked by Adrien Rabiot and Yunus Musah in a midfield three, though the Frenchman could play a bit further forward. Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are the wingers either side of Goncalo Ramos.

We have become accustomed to line-ups appearing a certain way and being used differently under Amorim though, so there may be some surprises compared to how the team looks on paper.

The bench features the likes of Pavlovic, Ardon Jashari, Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse and Francesco Camarda, all of whom will hope to be able to lend a hand in a winning cause if called upon.

Official Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Bench: Pittarella, Torriani, Estupinan, Hutchinson, Comotto, Jashari, Pavlovic, F. Terracciano, Cisse, Camarda.

Official Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Citizens, Calvani, Monterisi; Oyono, Calò, Masini, Tchato; Schmidt; Ghedjemis, Kvernadze.

Bench: Pisseri, Desplanches, Amey, Birligea, Cichella, Zerbin, Akpoguma, El Azzouzi, Fini, Hasa, Terzic, Fayed, Bobcek.

Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: “Surprising” Mauricio Pochettino decision called out as "negligent" Red Devils slump to upcoming low

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 11:22.
  • Manchester United's hierarchy have been accused of negligence by former captain Gary Neville after failing to strengthen their defence during the summer transfer window.
  • The Red Devils slumped to a concerning latest low as they suffered a humbling 4-0 defeat against rivals Liverpool on Sunday, leaving them 19th in the Premier League table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 11:22.

Manchester United's hierarchy have been accused of negligence by former captain Gary Neville after failing to strengthen their defence during the summer transfer window.

The Red Devils slumped to a concerning latest low as they suffered a humbling 4-0 defeat against rivals Liverpool on Sunday, leaving them 19th in the Premier League table.

New head coach Mauricio Pochettino became the first boss in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his opening match in charge of a club.

Liverpool took advantage of Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card and ran riot on Merseyside, with goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz condemning the Red Devils to their fifth league loss of the season.

Man United have posted only one win in 11 league games this season, while they have now conceded 34 goals across all competitions – the highest total of any team across Europe's top-five divisions.

It has been revealed that commenting on Man United’s defensive woes as a pundit for Sky Sports, Neville remarked: "It's negligent. The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years.".

Man United instead opted to prioritise a midfield rebuild, with Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans all brought in for a combined fee in the region of £150m.

Pochettino’s nightmare start to life as Man United boss could not have gone much worse, and his decision to hand Matthias de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days has been called into question by Neville.

The Dutch defender, who recently recovered from a long-term injury, was partly at fault for the first goal conceded by the Red Devils, misjudging a high ball that led to Yoro’s red card, and he was run ragged by Liverpool’s pacey frontline all afternoon.

"[Myself and Jamie Carragher] were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," stated Neville.

"I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes. Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.

"Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt. Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.

Industry observers note that "I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como (4-1 defeat in the Champions League), he was all over the place in Como. It's almost like you don't know what's happening.

In a recent development, "I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well. I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either.".

While Neville believes that a back four of Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw (right now injured) represents the “best” back four for Man United, playing with other defensive combinations will see the club get relegated.

"You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," Neville added. "A few weeks ago against Fulham, I said it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.

"At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact. The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.".

He continued: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Martinez.

Recent findings suggest that "Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.

"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.

"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact.".

Man United’s total of just eight Premier League points after 11 matches is their lowest at this stage of a top-flight season since 1972-73, but Pochettino’s side are only one point adrift of safety heading into their next league fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

Published: 04:11 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 03:04 EST, 19 November 2026.

Harry Kane is one of the main contenders for the prestigious Best Men's Player prize at the Globe Soccer Awards - and you can vote for the winner.

The Ballon d'Or king is joined by England team-mates Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, and Bukayo Saka in the category.

Meanwhile, Lionesses star Alessia Russo is the sole English representative in contention for the Best Women's Player honour.

Voting is now open across 12 categories, with the awards to be handed out at a glitzy ceremony in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on December 28.

The Globe Soccer Awards began in 2010 and have since become popular among fans worldwide, with more than 100 million votes cast in some years.

Last year's winner Ousmane Dembele is also in the running for Best Men's Player, with Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe joining him in the 26-strong shortlist.

Harry Kane, pictured with the Ballon d'Or, is among the nominees for Best Men's PLayer at the Globe Soccer Awards.

Voting is now open across 12 award categories ahead of a ceremony in Dubai in December.

Erling Haaland won the Best Men's Player prize for 2023 and is in contention again.

Premier League stars Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, William Saliba, and Dominik Szoboszlai are also hoping to get their hands on the prize.

Mikel Arteta and Unai Emery are in the running for Best Coach, while Myles Lewis-Skelly and Nico O'Reilly are competing for the Emerging Player gong.

There are 14 categories, with a 'Career and Special Awards' section yet to see its talent announced.

Arsenal are hopefuls in the Best Club category for both men and women, with Aston Villa joining them in the former and Manchester City in the latter.

There will also be prizes for the best forward, midfielder, defender, and goalkeeper, and Fans' Historic Club, Best Sporting Director, and Best Agent.

In a recent development, ronaldo, a serial winner at the ceremony, is defending his Best Middle East Player crown after winning his first Saudi Pro League title with Al-Nassr. Ivan Toney is among his rivals for that.

Fans are able to cast their votes until November 30, after which a jury including the likes of Antonio Conte and Luis Figo will also have their say.

It is an event of truly global interest, with supporters from more than 225 countries having cast votes in previous editions.

'We are incredibly proud to return for our third consecutive year as title partner of the GLOBE SOCCER Awards,' said Adil Taqi, CEO of title sponsor BEYOND Developments.

'Our continued partnership reflects BEYOND Developments’ commitment to connecting with an international audience through shared passions and experiences.

'Football brings people together across cultures and borders, resonating with our belief in pushing boundaries and aiming higher, a mindset shared by the players, coaches and clubs who will be honoured this December. We are proud to stand alongside an event that unites the global football family.'.

Fans are able to vote via the Globe Soccer App.

Tech Report: Leny Yoro: How many Man United games will defender miss after "unfair" red card in humbling defeat at Liverpool?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:30, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 08:31.
  • Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is forced to serve a suspension following his early red card in Sunday’s heavy 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in the Premier League.
  • The 21-year-old defender was named in Mauricio Pochettino’s first starting lineup as the upcoming Red Devils head coach, operating on the right side of a three-man defence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:30, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 08:31.

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is forced to serve a suspension following his early red card in Sunday’s heavy 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in the Premier League.

The 21-year-old defender was named in Mauricio Pochettino’s first starting lineup as the upcoming Red Devils head coach, operating on the right side of a three-man defence.

However, his afternoon came to an abrupt end inside the first eight minutes when he was shown a straight red card for a clumsy coming-together with Liverpool striker Alexander Isak on the edge of Man United’s penalty area.

Defensive partner Matthijs de Ligt – starting his first PL game in 357 days – misjudged a high ball by Ronald Araujo, which gifted Isak a free run towards goal before Yoro brought him down as the last man.

According to recent reports, at the time of the incident, referee Sam Barrott said on-field: "It's a red card for DOGSO (denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity). On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO," to which VAR added: "Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul.".

The Premier League Match Centre then explained the decision, posting on X: "The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR.".

It has been revealed that leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! ? https://t.co/VKYvckvBBP.

This is the second time that Yoro has been sent off for Man United this season, having previously been giving his marching orders in a 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid in October for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Yoro’s dismissal at Anfield was immediately punished, as Dominik Szoboszlai fired home the resulting free kick, before Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead less than three minutes later.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz then got their names on the scoresheet in the second half to help Liverpool secure a comfortable victory against a Red Devils outfit that sit down in 19th place in the Premier League table after 11 games.

Yoro will now serve a one-match suspension in the Premier League, forcing him to miss next Saturday’s clash against Brentford at Old Trafford, before he is free to return for a trip to Newcastle United on December 2.

Red cards for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity - a non-violent offence - carries a standard one-game domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban.

Before the Red Devils face Brentford, they will take on Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday and Yoro is available to play for Pochettino’s side in that game, as he served his UCL ban in the previous fixture against Roma at the start of the month.

According to recent reports, pochettino led a chorus of complaints that Yoro was given an “unfair” red card at Anfield, telling Sky Sports: "So painful. So disappointed. It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Sources indicate that "The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

"We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.".

According to recent reports, pressed on whether he was unhappy with Isak's heavy touch, Pochettino: "The ball was for the goalkeeper (Senne Lammens). In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional.".

Man United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with his new manager, adding: "The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

"No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper. They're both running full speed. What can we do? It is what it is.

"It's 10 versus 11, you come to a place like Anfield, it's a tough game anyway. Then you lose a man, it makes it hard. I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game. We take the pain and move on.

Sources indicate that "I wouldn't say it all goes out the window. You can still take the things you did in training into the game, but it makes it 10 times harder with one less man in a situation like that.

"It's hard, it's painful. But no one's coming to save us. We have to work hard, keep digging, keep working, keep fighting. It will all come round.".

Meanwhile, Gary Neville has questioned one key decision made by Pochettino in his first Man United match and has hit out at the club’s 'negligent' hierarchy over their summer transfer dealings.

Milan Futuro kept up their excellent recent form by sweeping aside Tritium 3-0, continuing their push towards the top.

According to recent reports, the Futuro came into the game in good form, having won three on the spin. A thrilling 3-2 victory over Virtus Verona was followed by a 2-1 victory against Piacenza in the rescheduled suspended game, and then a 3-0 home win over Virtus CiseranoBergamo before the break put them two points off top.

It has been revealed that milan’s mission upon the resumption of Serie D was a quite simple one: to build on the three wins in a row and put some pressure on ChievoVerona at the top, a side that they beat away from home a few weeks ago. They faced a Tritium side who started the day second bottom, with just two wins so far.

It has been revealed that it could hardly have been a better start for the Rossoneri, as they took the lead after less than 13 minutes. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 06:08 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • The Premier League have ruled that referees made a staggering six incorrect decisions in the latest round of matches as officials endured their worst weekend of the season so far.
  • It was unanimously ruled that referee Farai Hallam should have awarded Kai Havertz a penalty after he was tugged in the area during Arsenal's victory over Hull City, despite being in an offside position.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 06:08 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 19 November 2026.

The Premier League have ruled that referees made a staggering six incorrect decisions in the latest round of matches as officials endured their worst weekend of the season so far.

It was unanimously ruled that referee Farai Hallam should have awarded Kai Havertz a penalty after he was tugged in the area during Arsenal's victory over Hull City, despite being in an offside position.

That is because the laws state that if a foul occurs before an offside offence, a penalty should be awarded.

Although Havertz was in an offside position, he had not committed an offence as he neither played the ball nor interfered with play.

The key match incidents panel (KMI) mentioned: 'Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded.'.

Farai Hallam's decision not to award Kai Havertz a penalty was deemed incorrect by the key match incidents panel.

Coventry were wrongly denied a spot-kick in their defeat to Everton after James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair.

1. Everton vs Coventry City: Frank Lampard's side should have been awarded a penalty when James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair.

According to recent reports, 2. Everton vs Coventry City: The Toffees' second goal, scored by Thierno Barry should not have stood as the ball was adjudged to have gone into the back of the net off his hand.

3. Arsenal vs Hull City: Kai Havertz was denied a penalty after being dragged down. The referee did not award a spot-kick because Havertz in an offside position. However, that decision was incorrect, as he was not committing an offside offence and a spot-kick should therefore have been awarded.

4. Crystal Palace vs Liverpool: Palace were awarded a penalty in the last minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool after Milos Kerkez and Dario Osario clashed heads in the penalty area. The panel saw this as a natural coming together.

5. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: A penalty was given after Abdoul Ouattara tumbled over. The referee gave a foul against Lewis Cook despite Ouattara stepping across him.

It has been revealed that 6. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: Marcus Tavernier should have seen a second yellow card for time-wasting.

They did, however, praise the VAR for asking the referee to review the incident on the monitor, even though Hallam stuck with his on-field call after watching it back.

In the same weekend, Tottenham Hotspur complained to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle's heavy challenge on Mathys Tel's ankle, which forced him off injured.

Spurs felt Bogle should have seen red, particularly after Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for a similar incident the week prior.

Reviewing the decision, the KMI panel were split but eventually concluded that the foul lacked 'the speed, force or intensity' to be considered serious foul play.

Two of the five panellists, however, felt that the challenge merited a red card.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace's consolation penalty in the 92nd minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool should never have been awarded.

The KMI panel unanimously agreed the referee was wrong to award a penalty when Milos Kerkez and Dario Osorio clashed heads while contesting the ball, with contact inevitable given both players were jumping.

However, VAR's decision not to intervene was supported because it was not a 'clear and obvious error'.

It is the second penalty incident in as many weeks that went against Liverpool after Alexander Isak was wrongfully denied a spot-kick against Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that on the opposite side of Merseyside, James Tarkowski was fortunate not to concede a penalty for pulling Caleb Yirenkyi's hair during Everton's win over Coventry City, with the score still 0-0 at the time. The panel found that Coventry should have been awarded a penalty while Tarkowski should have been booked.

Last season, that incident would likely have resulted in a straight red card. However, the guidance changed this term with red cards only brandished for excessive force.

Thierno Barry's goal that gave Everton the lead faced scrutiny as three panellists believed it should have been disallowed on the pitch, with the 'balance of probability suggesting the ball accidentally struck Barry's hand before directly entering the goal'.

There were also two incorrect decisions in Bournemouth's victory over Ipswich Town.

Bournemouth defender Marcus Tavernier should have been sent off for a second yellow card in the 96th minute for delaying the restart during their 2-1 win, the panel found. However, it was a close call as the panel voted 3-2 against the decision.

Ipswich's scored penalty was also deemed wrongly awarded, with Abdoul Ouattara stepping across Lewis Cook to win the spot-kick rather than being fouled by the defender.

The KMI panel consists of a representative from the Premier League and Pro Ref alongside three former managers or players and meets after every round of Premier League matches to evaluate significant refereeing decisions.

Ref boss Howard Webb will speak to Premier League clubs at a routine meeting on Thursday.

While the panel is not newly introduced, this is the first season their findings have been publicly released in Pro Ref's drive for greater transparency and accountability.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb is due to appear in front of clubs on Thursday at a routine Premier League meeting.

And in more positive news for Webb, he will be able to share that VAR delays are down this season after increasing the bar for interventions.

Meanwhile, the KMI panel have assessed 296 decisions this season - only six of which have been judged to be wrong post-VAR.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Tottenham Hotspur have received a major patch on the future of teenage starlet Luca Williams-Barnett.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:50.

Tottenham Hotspur have received a major patch on the future of teenage starlet Luca Williams-Barnett.

The highly-rated academy graduate, who turned 18 at the start of October, made a notable impression on his full debut for Spurs in a 2-0 Premier League home win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Williams-Barnett opened the scoring with his first senior goal in the 15th minute, arriving at the back post to poke the ball home, before a blistering dribble that began from inside his own half helped him to set up Dominic Solanke shortly after half time.

Tottenham’s youngest scorer in the Premier League since Gareth Bale in 2007 received a standing ovation from the home crowd and also picked up the Man of the Match award.

After making his first-team debut as a 16-year-old last season, calls for the skilful winger to get more minutes have only grown louder over a challenging 12 months at Spurs.

Ensuring that Williams-Barnett commits his future to the club has also been high on the agenda, with the youngster having now entered the final 24 months of his current deal.

However, football.london reports that Williams-Barnett has agreed to sign a upcoming long-term deal at Tottenham, seemingly cooling fears that he could leave to join a rival club.

The England Under-19 international has now featured four times in the senior Spurs side under head coach Roberto De Zerbi, who was full of praise for the “special” teenager after the win over Ipswich.

Industry observers note that "Luca is a special player,” De Zerbi told reporters post-match. "I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top teammates.

"I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my initiative, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be notable.

"The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom, and Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

"And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

"Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.".

After revealed that Williams-Barnett prepared for the game on the team bus by watching YouTube videos of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, De Zerbi was asked whether the Spurs starlet could reach the same level as Barcelona and Spain sensation Yamal, who finished third in the 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings.

De Zerbi replied: "Yes, I think so, and one of the best things in my career… I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

In a recent development, "I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?".

Williams-Barnett will hope to be rewarded with a second successive start when Tottenham travel to the Stadium of Light to face Sunderland in their next Premier League fixture on Sunday.

  • Recent findings suggest that "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

According to recent reports, on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

Recent findings suggest that "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

It has been revealed that neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

Recent findings suggest that it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the strategy to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

According to recent reports, we now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

According to recent reports, that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

According to recent reports, fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their new head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

Sources indicate that united’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

According to recent reports, manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

Recent findings suggest that but, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

Sources indicate that I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

In a recent development, michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Sources indicate that both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

In a recent development, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

Sources indicate that I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

Industry observers note that I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

Recent findings suggest that I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

Industry observers note that we wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so crucial for us.

There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

Recent findings suggest that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

Industry observers note that I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

It was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

In a recent development, it was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

The defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

Fulham kick off in the second half.

It has been revealed that at half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

United almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

According to recent reports, united’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

In a recent development, the game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

Recent findings suggest that mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

This stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

Recent findings suggest that fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Recent findings suggest that bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

Fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

Sources indicate that the interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

Fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

It has been revealed that bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

It has been revealed that fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Industry observers note that very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

It has been revealed that if Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

Sources indicate that subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

Here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

The script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick states Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a substantial impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager mentioned.

In a recent development, “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

Sources indicate that “But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he remarked it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and latest head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Reworded scientific phrases can thwart publishers’ plagiarism checkers, but, in many cases, the resulting combinations of words only draw more attention from scientific sleuths.
  • These days, I spend a lot of my time looking through published papers that I suspect are fraudulent.
  • It has been revealed that I retired in 2022 from the University of Oxford, UK, where I worked as a developmental neuropsychologist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reworded scientific phrases can thwart publishers’ plagiarism checkers, but, in many cases, the resulting combinations of words only draw more attention from scientific sleuths. Credit: Gregory Dubus/iStock via Getty.

These days, I spend a lot of my time looking through published papers that I suspect are fraudulent. It is a gruelling task. But amid the tedium, there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers. It’s hard not to smile when ‘breast cancer’ becomes ‘bosom peril’, or a citation for ‘Baker and Logue’ become ‘Pastry Specialist and Logue’.

It has been revealed that I retired in 2022 from the University of Oxford, UK, where I worked as a developmental neuropsychologist. I now track down research fraud as part of a community of scientific sleuths. We work together to identify papers that we consider to be problematic in some way, then send the evidence to publishers or post it on PubPeer, a post-publication peer-review platform. Our aim is for the problematic papers to be investigated and, if appropriate, retracted by their publishers. But, often, publishers are slower and more recalcitrant than many sleuths would like them to be.

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars.

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars.

Sources indicate that many people blame academia’s ‘publish or perish’ research culture for the rise in problematic papers. Without a large number of publications and citations, prospects for employment, promotion and glittering prizes evaporate. Some researchers cut corners, manipulate or fabricate data, or copy the work of other scientists without citing them.

The demand for desperate researchers to get their name on a publication in any journal has spawned semi-professional organizations known as paper mills. These sell authorship status, with prices that vary depending on the impact factor of the journal. Articles are typically generated using artificial-intelligence tools or plagiarized, and tend to find homes in journals that lack sufficient editorial scrutiny.

According to recent reports, one of the few amusing consequences of these developments is the phenomenon of tortured phrases, first described in 2021 by computer scientists Guillaume Cabanac and Cyril Labbé and software engineer Alexander Magazinov1. They analysed huge volumes of research literature to identify patterns. Tortured phrases arise when someone — or, in most cases, a computer — replaces words in a published article with synonyms to evade plagiarism detectors and ultimately publish the result as their own work.

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work.

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work.

Cabanac and colleagues developed a free website called the Problematic Paper Screener, which documents tortured phrases and other red flags in publications. Detection of tortured phrases has been a communal effort by research sleuths, who document specific articles with tortured phrases on PubPeer.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03040-z.

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 09:01.

It has been revealed that with the serious injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, PSG are expected to look to strengthen in the January transfer window. An ideal profile has been identified and two targets have already been ruled out.

Sources indicate that it is a double blow for PSG. Desire Doue has joined Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the treatment room, probably until the end of the season, as both Paris attackers have suffered cruciate ligament ruptures.

While the signing of an attacker was already being considered after the Georgian's injury, it now seems necessary with the French player's, which was added this weekend.

According to Le Parisien, the decision-makers at the capital club are nevertheless split between trusting the current squad and not compromising the rest of the season.

Luis Enrique does have solutions to cover for these two notable absences with Senny Mayulu, Ferran Torres, Maghnes Akliouche, Mika Godts or Quentin Ndjantou.

Luis Campos will be attentive to opportunities in January, with a specific player profile in mind: a versatile attacking player, more of a winger than a centre-forward. To match Luis Enrique's expectations, he will need to be comfortable in tight spaces, capable of provoking and dominating his opponent one-on-one.

The same source indicates that Eli Junior Kroupi and Paris Brunner, who are nevertheless two highly sought-after gems, do not have the profile PSG are looking for this January. They are therefore two options to be set aside. Finding the ideal player will be no easy task in the January transfer window, as the massive European clubs will not be inclined to part with an important player mid-season.

Sources indicate that moreover, Paris no longer wish to overpay for their signings, despite this extraordinary situation. The Paris hierarchy therefore have six weeks before the January transfer window opens to deepen their search and potentially find the perfect player. Between now and January 2027, Luis Enrique, for his part, will be able to assess his attacking resources and try to maintain a good level of performance.

Tech Report: Inside Xabi Alonso's goalkeeping headache: Why Blues boss could go against the fans' view and pick volatile Emiliano Martinez over 21-year-old prodigy Mike Penders

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (861 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 05:36 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:52 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.
  • One is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 05:36 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:52 EST, 19 November 2026.

A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

One is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career. The other is a 34-year-old Argentinian who won the 2022 World Cup and has appeared 234 times in the Premier League.

According to recent reports, we mention those brief backgrounds because when assessing who will give him the greater chance of stopping Leeds United from scoring on Saturday, Xabi Alonso takes them into account. Indeed, Alonso told us so while covering Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

One conversation with the manager was centred on his goalkeeper options. At that time, they were Penders and Robert Sanchez.

In a recent development, alonso praised Penders’ potential but explained to us how highly he values ‘experience’ in his goalkeeper. ‘To have this security in goal is notable,’ he insisted when asked.

It has been revealed that sanchez was indeed nominated as his No 1 for their first fixture of the Premier League season at Fulham. The 29-year-old Spaniard had a stinker, which led to him being loaned to Como. It is a straightforward loan, and he has been second-choice to Jean Butez under Cesc Fabregas, so there is a chance he will be back at Chelsea next summer, but that is a problem for another day.

A Daily Mail Sport poll of almost 2,000 Chelsea fans resulted in 57.9 per cent voting in favour of Mike Penders (above) keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

Martinez is available for the first time since breaking his jaw at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

In a recent development, martinez arrived from Aston Villa for £7.5million, was told he would be Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, and is now available again. He is able to play without a protective mask, as he did while representing Argentina in their 7-0 friendly win over Costa Rica on Tuesday night.

It was his first appearance since breaking his jaw at Everton and having surgery exactly a month prior. He headed back to London after that victory to return to Chelsea, presumably under the impression that he will be playing against Leeds come Saturday.

In a recent development, it is Alonso who will have the ultimate say on who goes in goal, in conjunction with his head of goalkeeping, Ben Roberts, and assistant goalkeeping coach, James Russell. That decision will be communicated with his chosen goalkeeper in the build-up, though Alonso is unlikely to tell us when we ask him at his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

One insider consulted this week mentioned his suspicion is the Argentinian will make an immediate return because it would create a headache for Alonso. Martinez is a big character, volatile, and, if reduced to second choice, would not be pleased.

Statistically, Leeds cross the ball more than most in the Premier League, which could be more challenging for Penders than Martinez.

Filling in for Martinez, Penders punched the ball into his own goal on his first league start for Chelsea in a 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur.

It has been revealed that however, he impressed against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, then Manchester United and Sunderland in the Premier League. He won the Save of the Month award for October for denying Bryan Mbeumo at Stamford Bridge.

Penders won October's Save of the Month award for denying Man United's Bryan Mbeumo.

In a recent development, penders is clearly a terrific talent, and it would be tempting to continue to show trust in him by having him face Leeds. Chelsea then face Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace, Liverpool and Manchester City in a rush of fixtures as we head into December.

It is a significant decision to be made by Alonso, and would take bravery for him to stick with his prodigy in Penders, when we know the experience of the proven Martinez weighs heavy in his mind.

Chelsea vice captain Moises Caicedo is to be checked over at Cobham after a small injury scare while the influential midfielder was away with Ecuador.

Caicedo would be expected to wear the armband at Leeds in Reece James’ ongoing absence. He is set to return to the training ground on Thursday to be assessed.

In a recent development, the 25-year-old played 84 minutes in Ecuador’s first fixture of the break, a 2-0 victory against Costa Rica in which he scored. However, he then asked to be substituted at half-time of their 2-0 win over Bolivia, which ended in the early hours of Wednesday morning. Captaining his country, it was believed to be due to a small physical complaint.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Chelsea have been looking at the midfield market in the build-up to this January after they missed out on bolstering their options in the summer when Enzo Fernandez was sold to Manchester City. They retain an interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

Match gallery: Bognor Regis Town Women too hot for AFC Varsity

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bognor took the lead on three minutes as Carter set up Hunphrey on the wing and she placed it low to Delillis, who diverted it in at the near post.
  • Alice Gue was fouled outside the area.
  • Sources indicate that nicole Robinson had to stop Dot Usher’s attempt at the other end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bognor took the lead on three minutes as Carter set up Hunphrey on the wing and she placed it low to Delillis, who diverted it in at the near post.

Alice Gue was fouled outside the area. Up stepped Niamh Andersson to take the free-kick but she sent it just over.

Sources indicate that nicole Robinson had to stop Dot Usher’s attempt at the other end. Then Carter squared the ball towards Freya Boxer but she was put off by a defender.

Boxer spotted the keeper off her line and struck it from the far right but it rolled wide. Bognor had to defend with Usher causing problems and two strikes led to two good saves from Robinson.

Bognor extended their lead on 13 minutes as a defence-splitting pass set up Humphrey and she timed her run well before blasting it high into the net.

Sources indicate that carter had two long range efforts that bounced wide soon after. Lou Selvester's 22nd minute corner dipped into the heart of the area but Delillis couldn't quite control it and Lottie Tough gathered it.

Usher hit the Rockettes on the break and put in a perfect pass for Freya Lines who sped through the middle but her strike was well saved by Robinson.

It has been revealed that humphrey ran through and unselfishly played it across the box for Boxer to have a go but she struck it wide. Sophia Poling was late in a tackle on the left flank and was shown a yellow card in first half stoppage time.

Early in the second half, Andersson had a shot from long distance but that flew wide. Aliyah Bower hit the side netting from outside the box on 50 minutes at the other end. Delillis had the ball in the net after Carter's through ball but was ruled offside. Macie Downs won a corner with her long throw into the box but a Varsity defender headed away.

Lou Lou Robson came on for Sophia Poling and soon had to head a corner clear before Jess Nunn's strike was saved by Robinson.

Bognor got their third on 63 minutes as Delillis played a pass through defence to Humphrey and she ran into the box and sent the ball to the back post where Carter was waiting to smash it in.

It has been revealed that abbie Akhopie hit a dangerous cross into the area and Robinson had to save before Carter cleared the rebound. Clara Castanheira replaced Gue for the Rockettes then Andersson set up Boxer, but with only the keeper to beat, she fired wide.

Selvester's corner fell to Delillis and she struck the crossbar before Andersson smashed wide on the follow-up.

In a recent development, bognor concede on 75 minutes as Akhopie sped through following a long ball and fired it in. Soon Delillis played it inside for Humphrey who turned and composed herself but shot wide.

Sources indicate that bower hit a long range free-kick at goal but Robinson denied her. On 80 minutes Poppy Shine replaced Robinson in goal for Bognor. Then on 83 minutes, Boxer came off for Talliah Anderson.

On 93 minutes Andersson came off for Chloe Blanks in Bognor's final change.

Bognor’s win leaves them second, three points behind leaders Havant with a game in hand.

The Rockettes travel to AFC Portchester Reserves on Sunday (November 29, 2pm) before welcoming Guernsey to Nyewood Lane on Sunday, December 6 (1pm).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:13.

European football returns to the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday evening, when Arsenal welcome a Borussia Dortmund side just one point below them in the Champions League rankings.

The Gunners have navigated their opening four matches unbeaten to collect 10 points and sit third in the table, while Niko Kovac's side have lost one and won three in the continent's top tier so far to lie 12th.

Here, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

It has been revealed that arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund is scheduled for an 8pm kickoff on Tuesday, November 24.

Another six matches will commence at the same time, including Manchester City vs. Napoli and Real Madrid vs. PSV Eindhoven.

Arsenal are hosting Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, where Mikel Arteta's men have won each of their first six games in all tournaments this season, conceding just two goals in the process.

BVB last visited Arsenal's home turf in 2014, when Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez propelled the Gunners to a 2-0 group-stage victory.

It has been revealed that arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund will not be shown on terrestrial television in the UK; instead, the fixture will be broadcast on Amazon Prime Video.

Fans with an Amazon Prime Video subscription can watch the game on a variety of devices, such as via the TV app, phones, computers and games consoles.

Amazon Prime Video costs £8.99 a month for the full Amazon Prime package, or £7.99 a month for just Amazon Prime Video, although the latter is only available to select accounts.

Highlights of the match will be made available on the Amazon Prime and TNT Sports YouTube channels shortly after full time, as well as the official Arsenal account.

The @primevideosport X account will also post short clips of key moments as and when they happen.

Top spot in the Champions League table is within Arsenal's reach, as the third-placed Gunners are just two points behind Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, the latter of whom do not take to the field until Wednesday vs. Roma.

Arteta's men will therefore rise to first for at least 24 hours if they win and Real Madrid lose to PSV, or if they triumph, Los Blancos draw and Arsenal also make up a -1 goal difference to Jose Mourinho's side.

The Gunners could also equal two Champions League records, as they are a win or draw away from matching their longest-ever run of unbeaten group stage/league phase games (17) and could also draw level with Liverpool's English record of 13 consecutive group stage/league phase wins at home.

On the other hand, Dortmund are capable of rising into the top eight automatic qualification places with a shock win in North London, but head coach Kovac has only won one of his previous five Champions League matches against an English club; a 7-2 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur with Bayern Munich in 2019.

Limitless started the brighter, dominating possession in the opening 10 minutes of this Sussex Junior Cup third round tie, before Goring gradually took control of the game with the midfield trio of Todor Bankov, Nathan Madgwick and Bambo carving out several chances for a front three of Connor Pomeroy, Ben Rubano and Luke Tate. Limitless kept Goring at bay until the 31st minute when Bambo fed Rubano whose clever flick found man of the match Connor Pomeroy who drove home from the edge of the box to give Goring a 1-0 lead. It has been revealed that on 43 minutes a fine pass from Bankov found Pomeroy and his shot from just inside the box was very well saved by the home keeper. From the resultant corner, Luke Tate found Rubano who curled a delightful shot into the top corner to give Goring a well deserved 3-0 lead at half time.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes insists the prospect of lifting the Premier Sports Cup in the coming weeks has his squad operating with laser-like focus, with Saturday’s dramatic late victory over Motherwell providing a further boost to their growing belief that trophies are within reach.

There is still plenty of work to be done before the Rangers can contemplate silverware, but McInnes believes a shot at Hampden glory is acting as an added incentive for his players and is helping to drive standards inside the dressing room.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Before their return trip to the national stadium on December 13, Rangers must navigate a favourable-looking sequence of home fixtures, with Aberdeen, Falkirk and Dundee United all due to visit Ibrox over the next eight days in the Scottish Premiership.

While the cup final represents an obvious carrot and a major opportunity for silverware is fast approaching, McInnes knows it is impossible for his players to ignore the occasion altogether. However, he is equally determined to ensure their focus remains on the immediate task in hand, claiming performances over the next four league fixtures could determine who earns the right to feature when the substantial occasion arrives.

Industry observers note that speaking after his side kept their Premiership title assault firmly on track with a last-gasp success at Fir Park, McInnes said: “I don't think I'll mention it too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team. Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

“We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to come away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward, but there's bigger games like a cup final looming, so everybody wants to play in that one. I'm sure it does us no harm. It keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully we're in good form.”.

If the celebrations following Ryan Naderi’s scrappy 88th-minute winner against the Steelmen were anything to go by, a turbo-charged belief is surging through the Rangers ranks as they look to end a two-season trophy drought.

Such resilience is invaluable in a title challenge and McInnes is encouraged by that quality, but stressed the need for greater consistency in his side’s performance levels leading to those decisive moments.

In a recent development, “I think we're the only team in the Premier League who's not lost away from home, but we understand that draws won't get the job done,” he stated. “Last-minute winners are brilliant. They're normally aligned with successful teams and they can get so many points from that. It's good to know that we've got that but, like I say, I wouldn't want to be depending on it far too often.”.

According to recent reports, the importance of Rangers’ upcoming run of home fixtures is not lost on McInnes. While the jubilant scenes at full-time in North Lanarkshire were particularly satisfying, there was little time to revel in the celebrations with Aberdeen arriving at Ibrox on Tuesday night.

The Dons will venture back down the A90 in buoyant mood after giving new boss Mario Frick a winning start to his Pittodrie tenure with a 4-2 victory over bottom club Kilmarnock at the weekend.

According to recent reports, the long-standing rivalry between the clubs leaves McInnes in no doubt that his side face another demanding test against his former club. Nevertheless, he is relishing a return to familiar surroundings after a run of five consecutive away matches.

He is equally aware, however, that home advantage alone offers no guarantee of success.

Sources indicate that “It's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,” McInnes noted. “We've got some good fixtures at home but we always look at little blocks in the week, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, get certain points and certain targets.

It has been revealed that “There was obviously a lot of joy and pleasure with that [Motherwell result], but it wasn't over the top. When we spoke after the game, it was about getting ourselves ready for Aberdeen. We all know the historical rivalry between both clubs. I’m sure they'll come to Ibrox with a bit of confidence getting the result [against Kilmarnock]. We need to be ready for that.

“We’ve got a significant week ahead of us. and we've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game I'll be happy.”.

City made just one change to the starting XI that had thumped Hassocks 6-0 in midweek.

In a recent development, skipper Rob Hutchings began at left-back with Zac Jeaneson the other side of Ben Pashley and Will Sweet in the heart of the defence. Max Evans was between the posts and Joe Moore, Lucas Pattenden, Isaac Bello, Joe Clarke and Emmett Dunn started in midfield with Harry Bridle up front.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Ethan Prichard, Olly Munt, Finn Bello, Lloyd Rowlatt and Brandon Chebby warmed the bench.

Dunn brought down Dan Bayliss for a ‘Stoke free kick and Kristian Shevchenko, son of Dynamo Kyiv, AC Milan and Chelsea legend Andriy Shevchenko, was flagged offside.

Basingstoke’s Amardeep Singh blazed over the bar before Pashley blocked a shot and another one was diverted for the first corner of the afternoon. Joe O’Loughlin took it and Shevchenko headed wide.

Another shot went off target in the ninth minute as Chi struggled to get going, but the hosts won their first corner 60 seconds later and Jeanes fired one wide.

Hutchings earned City a set-piece up against Okine-Peters and Pattenden and Jeanes hooked up for a cross that Bello couldn’t profit from, and Pattenden had a shot blocked.

Clarke headed away a free kick after Hutchings fouled Shevchenko and O’Loughlin delivered it into the box.

Basingstoke keeper Tyla Dickinson made a mistake on 16 minutes but no one was there to capitalise.

Evans claimed Scott Armsworth’s header before a dangerous cross was headed out for a Lillywhites’ goal kick and Stoke captain Billy Upton missed an opportunity.

Thomas Blake was replaced by James Henry for the visitors, and a Bello bomb of a throw was debuted after Pattenden battled with O’Loughlin, although Dickinson collected at the second time of asking.

It has been revealed that skipper Hutchings’ cross was claimed by Dickinson on the half hour and Singh was given the first yellow card for taking out Hutchings. A poor cross from Pattenden didn’t cause the visitors any trouble before referee Joshua Langley-Fineing sent Shevchenko off for raising an arm on Hutchings in the 37th minute.

In a recent development, bridle couldn’t pick out Bello and Pattenden won a corner that Hutchings took, and Sweet turned the loose ball in to put City one up on 41. Bridle struck a shot off target as the half petered out.

The City striker had another chance soon after the break before the away side equalised on 51 through Okine-Peters at close range from a cross via the left wing.

Chi won a couple of corners and Bridle somehow had an effort saved following good work between Bello and Pattenden.

The away side might have taken the lead after a Pashley slip but Evans blocked Okine-Peters’ shot. Then a super header from Dunn put Chi in front on the hour – his third goal of the week after two at Hassocks.

Jack Ball pulled an attempt wide in the 65th minute; and Dunn headed wide. Three minutes later ‘Stoke delivered a corner too deep.

Bayliss was booked for dissent and Hutchings got done on 76 and the visitors earned a corner that was headed away. A calamity led to the equaliser as Okine-Peters made it all square.

Chebby came on for Jeanes as Miles Rutherford and co rejigged, and Bello dropped back into defence.

The Chi sub was outmuscled by D’Andre Brown, and a penalty claim on Stoke sub Cheick Sylla was waved away by the referee.

Munt replaced Moore and a header from Clarke was deflected for a City corner.

Evans saved a speculative effort from long distance at the other end and somehow denied Henry with a brilliant save as we entered five extra minutes.

Chinedu Agu was booked for pulling back Huthchings and Bello did well to prevent Agu getting in on 93 minutes.

Ball entered the ref’s notepad just before full-time.
