Celtic midfielder Benjamin Nygren is on the radar of Atalanta and Bologna, according to reports in Italy.

Nygren joined Celtic from FC Nordsjaelland in the summer of 2025 for a fee in the region of £1.5 million and made a big impact, scoring 21 goals across all competitions as the champions retained their Premiership crown and also lifted the Scottish Cup.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The 25-year-old also represented Sweden earlier this year at the World Cup and remains an integral part of Graham Potter’s international squad.

Recent findings suggest that this season, Nygren has netted eight times in 21 games. And with the January transfer window approaching, it is understood that two Serie A clubs in Atalanta and Bologna are weighing up a bid for Nygren.

Respected Italian transfer journalist Gianluca di Marzio has claimed in an interview with Rekatochklart that a move could be made for Nygren on the back of his performances over the past 18 months,.

“Nygren is a very good player and Atalanta like him a lot, but they haven’t made a move for him yet,” stated Di Marzio. “He is a target and they are following him.

“Bologna like him too, but no negotiations have started yet. They follow him because he is doing very well both for Celtic and Sweden.”.

Bologna have taken an active interest over the past few years in the Scottish market, signing defender Aaron Hickey from Hearts and midfielder Lewis Ferguson from Aberdeen.

Atalanta were also very interested in Matt O’Riley before the Celtic midfielder moved to Brighton and Hove Albion rather than Serie A in 2024.

Nygren admitted in September that there was interest in him after the World Cup this summer, although nothing materialised for the Swede.

Sources indicate that “Yeah, there was interest,” he said. “Was it more than that? No, I play for a significant club. When the right time is to move on, I cannot answer that. That’s up to me, the club and the potential club. So whenever the right time is, it is.

“I play for a huge club like Celtic. I really enjoy being here. I wanted to stay here to play in the biggest competition. Unfortunately, we didn’t make it to the Champions League, but we still play in the Europa League. I want to make it better here and then go further in the Europa League that we did last season.

Sources indicate that “I wanted to stay here and continue to make it good and when the right time is, the right time is. But it’s not something I think of now. It’s not my focus. My focus is just to do as well as possible here and to win more trophies and then what happens in the future, we’ll see.”.

Nygren is contracted to Celtic until 2030 and the Premiership leaders would likely demand a hefty fee for his services.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite another brace for a red-hot Nicole Mackay, Worthing Women were edged out in a five-goal ding-dong at Eastbourne Borough.

There was some good news pre-match with the return of Captain Holly Talbut-Smith, in the only change to the starting line-up from last week’s win over Aylesford. Kendall Varitek also came back in for Ludmila De Sousa on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Aiming to build on three precious points achieved at home the previous Sunday, the Rebels travelled East to the Connect Management Stadium to face bottom-of-the-table Borough, although it was the struggling hosts who almost caught their guests by surprise in under a minute. Isobel Langridge sent in a cross that had goalkeeper Sian Woods backtracking to palm the ball to safety.

Moments later, the visitors retaliated by way of Neve McEvaddy releasing the nippy Jess Richardson through the inside-right channel who, in turn, picked out Nicole Mackay for a shot which flashed across the face of goal.

The same player went close again when a lucky break in the box failed to extend to Mackay, as her effort went wide once more.

However, Worthing’s number nineteen wouldn't be denied for much longer.

Richardson won a free-kick in a central position around twenty yards from goal and up stepped the Red’s top scorer to fire home the set-piece via a deflection, which wrong-footed Sophia Moule between the home posts.

The lead was nearly doubled shortly afterwards, only for the crossbar to keep out Mackay following a flicked header applied to a deadball delivery from McEvaddy.

Borough bit back via a misplaced pass providing an opening for Langridge to land a long ranger on top of the net, around the half-hour mark.

Then some excellent defending by first, returning Skipper Talbut-Smith resulted in Molly Hill being ushered away from the target, allowing netminder Woods to pounce on the ball and complete the clean up operation.

A presentable chance offered an opportunity to an unmarked Richardson in the penalty area in the closing stages of the first forty-five, though the fleet-footed winger couldn’t keep her attempt down.

McEvaddy was forced off at the break, to be replaced by Varitek but it would be the Reds of Eastbourne Borough who came out of the blocks quickest after the turnaround.

A mere three minutes into the second-half, Lola Dulake located the dome of Hill, who offered Worthing a possible mountain to climb by heading home to level the score.

Steepness then nearly became the order of the day, thanks to Hill coming mighty close to doubling her tally and putting her side in front within a matter of seconds.

Industry observers note that showing no signs of letting up, Hill, who else ? was inches away again when she put a good chance over the apparatus, before the deadly duo of Dulake and Hill linked up to devastating effect to extend the homesters’ advantage, just shy of the hour.

The former crossed from the right and the latter gleefully gobbled up the opportunity to nod in her brace.

Roles were slightly reversed at the point Duklake fizzed a low attempt dangerously close to the target and Woods was called into action to repel a close-range effort, as the home team threatened to pull clear of their beleaguered opponents.

Dulake turned Ella Terry but could only find the hands of Woods, by which time Skye Birkinshaw had entered the fray in place of youngster Hattie Rainey, as Manager Jesus Cordon and his Coaching Staff tried to find a way back into the contest for the underfire travellers.

Fellow substitute Daisy Taylor almost had the opposite effect, as her long distance rocket forced a fine diving save out of Woods, at the expense of a corner.

A through ball might have put the game beyond Worthing’s reach, had Woods not had her wits about her to race out of her goal to intercept and smother at the feet of the hat-trick hunting Hill.

Six minutes from the end of ninety, Hill claimed the matchball by getting the better of Terry and gaining added purchase on an effort which crashed off the underside of the crossbar and fell the right slide of the line, for Borough.

Not letting their heads drop though, Rebels let out a yell when Mackay made it five goals in her last three games, as she swivelled on the edge of the eighteen yard box to beat Moule and set up a tense conclusion.

Unfortunately however, three-two to an understandably elated Eastbourne saw them collect only their second league win of the campaign, although, with just four points separating the bottom five clubs, nobody is safe.

Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026.

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live.

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release.

According to recent reports, in a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and showed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'.

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The upcoming boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

It has been revealed that alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'.

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

Industry observers note that 'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'.

Recent findings suggest that it’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9.

Conor McGregor unveiled that he would give employees at various businesses the day off.

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern.

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the new GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

In a recent development, he told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'.

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the new game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor declared that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was debuted.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

Sources indicate that 'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'.

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game.

According to recent reports, 'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, mentioned with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a major one.'.

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

Sources indicate that 'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' said Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'.

In a recent development, fresh York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall mentioned. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'.

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

Sources indicate that A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the matter as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'.

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after substantial games.

Those problems appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony said it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event.

Department store chain John Lewis noted it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 09:20.

Gameweek five in the Champions League sees Manchester City and Napoli square off in the League Phase.

These two teams suffered contrasting results in the previous round of fixtures, and here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into to their latest encounter.

Recent findings suggest that man City vs. Napoli will kick off at 20:00 UK time on Tuesday night.

This contest is one of nine taking place on the same evening, with Man City’s English rivals Arsenal among those also in action at home to Borussia Dortmund.

This Champions League match will take place at Man City’s home the Etihad Stadium, which now holds a capacity of 61,470 spectators following a recent expansion.

Man City have lost only two of their last 27 home fixtures in the group stage/League Phase of the Champions League (W22 D3), though one of those was earlier this season against holders Paris Saint-Germain (4-2).

According to recent reports, man City vs. Napoli will be shown live on TNT Sports 1 or TNT Sports Ultimate for viewers in the UK.

Fans with the TNT Sports package through their TV provider can watch this game on Sky Go and Virgin TV Go, while this fixture will also be streamed live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK, and on CBS on Paramount+ in the USA.

In a recent development, match highlights of Man City vs. Napoli will be available on Amazon Prime Video, TNT Sports and via BBC Sport’s dedicated UEFA Champions League Match of the Day show which you can watch live or stream on BBC iPlayer.

You can also view this match on the TNT Sports YouTube channel and both clubs' official YouTube accounts.

At the halfway stage in the League Phase, Man City sit seventh in the 36-team standings after accumulating nine points from their opening four matches.

Enzo Maresca’s side will realistically need at least a couple more victories to ensure they finish inside the top eight and secure automatic qualification for the last 16, rather than slip into the playoffs.

The Citizens have won each of their last three Champions League meetings with Napoli, most recently winning 2-0 on home soil in the League Phase of last season’s competition courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku.

Napoli will therefore be out for revenge when they make the trip back to the blue side of Manchester, while Wednesday’s fixture also marks the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne, whose first comeback to the Etihad was cut short.

Indeed, he was the unfortunate one sacrificed after just 21 minutes following a red card for Giovanni Di Lorenzo in Napoli's 2-0 defeat last season.

The Italian club have won one and lost three of their opening four UCL games this term, suffering a disappointing 4-1 defeat at Porto on November 4, and at the moment sit down in 27th place in the table, six points behind the top eight.

While Napoli enter this contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on Saturday, courtesy of a Scott McTominay goal, Man City were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham in the Premier League.

Two Scottish stadiums land World Cup matches as UK wins bid for 2035 Women’s finals

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hampden and Easter Road are set to host Women’s World Cup matches after England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 edition of the tournament.
  • The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hampden and Easter Road are set to host Women’s World Cup matches after England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 edition of the tournament.

The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It will be the first men’s or women’s World Cup finals to be staged in the UK since the 1966 men’s tournament was held in England.

It has been revealed that nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams. One of those venues – Old Trafford – has been included in its current guise but any rebuilt stadium is envisaged to be a host.

A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea stadium – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 stadiums across the four nations.

Scotland have two Candidate Stadiums - the national football arena Hampden (capacity 52,032), which was used as part of the delayed Euro 2020 men’s tournament in 2021, and Easter Road, the home of Hibs with a capacity of 20,093, that has never been used for a major tournament.

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold.

FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

The Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Commenting on confirmation that Scotland will co-host the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035, First Minister John Swinney said:.

"This is fantastic news for Scotland. We have proved time and again that we are a world-class host, and I am delighted that the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035 will be held in Scotland alongside England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

“The timing is ideal. Project 2035, our new long-term plan to grow the girls' and women's game, aims to establish Scotland as a leading nation for women's football by 2035. Our newly established girls’ and women’s football taskforce will help to make this happen, capitalising on the World Cup and leaving a lasting legacy for communities across the country.

Recent findings suggest that “Scotland is building a remarkable reputation for hosting major events, and the FIFA Women’s World Cup joins the Tour de France Grand Départ, The Open, the World Rally Championships and UEFA EURO 2028 in promising to showcase what our country has to offer. We will make sure each one of these amazing sporting events delivers for our economy, supporting jobs, businesses and tourism.”.

English Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the Congress after the bid’s success had been confirmed.

“Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035,” Hewitt said.

“We’re deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women’s football on behalf of the global football family.

“As we mentioned throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women’s World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.

“Together, we will celebrate the power of women’s football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women’s World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of.”.

The club stalwart has been put in temporary chatge at The Saffrons while the club look for a permanent replacement for Macdonald, whose axing alongside assistant Ben Davis has provoked an angry reaction from many fans and seen some players leave – includihg one who’d only rejoined the club on Friday.

The latest development at the Isthmian South East club came on Monday evening, when a club statement mentioned: “To serve for an interim period, Eastbourne Town F.C are pleased to announce the appointment of popular club stalwart Dave Winterton as First Team Manager.

"Dave is, of course, very well known to most people in the local area for his long and distinguished playing, coaching and management career with our club, and we sincerely thank him for agreeing to take on this role.

"During this time, Dave will be assisted by one of our experienced senior players, Arron Hopkinson. Our thanks also go to him.

"We hope that supporters will get behind Dave and the team during this period of transition, starting this coming Saturday away at Erith Town, whilst the search for a permanent successor to Jude Macdonald continues.”.

Dave is a second generation Winterton at Eastbourne Town – his father Derek played as a defender for the club in the 1950s.

He was club manager between June 2001 and January 2005, taking Town, who were playing in Division 2 of the Sussex League, into Division 1 and winning the Sussex Intermediate Cup. In 2020 Dave became the Goalkeeper coach for the club.

The move to make him interim boss comes after the surprise news on Saturday evening that Macdonald had been sacked with Town one off the bottom of the division but after two brighter league performances that had seen a point taken from each of two clashes with Sheppey and Whitstable.

Town’s statement on Saturday remarked: “Eastbourne Town FC have today parted company with First Team Manager Jude Macdonald and Ben Davis.

"The Committee would like to place on record their sincere thanks to Jude and Ben for their hard work over the last 4½ years, where, following their arrival, they quickly reshaped the remaining playing squad, and with some exciting latest arrivals, just two years later released an amazing mid-season recovery to storm up the SCFL Premier Division table to finish Runners-Up and then win the League Play-off Final.

"They then successfully kept the Club in the Isthmian F.L for successive seasons when largely up against many teams with much greater budgets and resources, a feat which we believe must be seen as a remarkable achievement in what is known by many to be a very tough division.

"The club wish them both all the very best for the future and thank them once again for their service during their time at The Saffrons. No further statements will be made at this time.”.

A number of Town fans have taken to social media to condemn Macdonald’s removal, calling it shocking and disgraceful.

At least a couple of players have left – including James Waters, who Macdonald had re-signed for the club only at the end of last week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland captain Caroline Weir says the country being named as a host nation for the 2035 Women’s World Cup is a “pivotal moment” for the sport.

The United Kingdom’s four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams.

According to recent reports, while the 2022 European Championships were held in England, Scotland has never hosted a major women’s football event. Hampden Park in Glasgow (capacity 52,032) and Hibs’ Easter Road in Edinburgh (capacity 20,093) are Scotland’s Candidate Stadiums and would stage at least group-stage matches. Weir feels that having the competition on Scotland’s doorstep will show youngsters in this country that “anything is possible”.

In a recent development, midfielder Weir, who presently plays for Lyon and has won 122 caps for Scotland, noted: “Hosting the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup in the UK is a pivotal moment for women’s football in this country. Playing at the 2019 Women’s World Cup in France was an incredible moment in my career, so knowing that the next generation of Scottish players will have the chance to experience that on home soil is so special.

“The women's game in Scotland has so much potential and this tournament is a real opportunity to drive momentum and help take it to another level both nationally and internationally.

“For young girls and boys across the country, seeing the best players in the world right on their doorstep will show them that anything is possible.

“We’re so proud to play our part in welcoming the world in 2035 and I know I speak on behalf of all of the players and staff when I say that we are ready to rise to the challenge and help deliver a truly memorable, world-class tournament.”.

Scottish Football chief executive Ian Maxwell hailed the decision to award the event to the UK. “Securing the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup alongside our Home Nations partners is a momentous milestone for Scottish football,” he noted. “Scotland has a proud footballing heritage and a rapidly growing women’s game, and welcoming the world to Barclays Hampden and Easter Road will turbo-charge the progress we have made across our grassroots, domestic, and international game.

It has been revealed that “This tournament will be the single-biggest sporting event ever staged in the UK, and our ambition goes far beyond the matches themselves. It gives us a powerful platform to inspire participation in a newly introduced generation of girls and women across Scotland, empower more female leaders and match officials and deliver a sustainable commercial and community legacy for many years to come.”.

It will be the first time that Easter Road, the home of Hibs, has been selected to host a major international event and the club say they are hugely excited at the prospect.

Hibs Women’s head coach Joelle Murray remarked: “This is fantastic news for women's football in Scotland and something we should all be extremely excited about.

It has been revealed that “To welcome the best players in the world to Easter Road would be incredibly special and provide a brilliant opportunity to showcase the women's game. It would also give young girls across the country the chance to experience a World Cup on their doorstep and to see what is possible to achieve through football.

“Having played and coached at Easter Road throughout my career, it holds a very special place in my heart. To see it named as a Candidate Stadium for a Women's World Cup is a hugely proud moment for me, and the opportunity to inspire the next generation makes it even more exciting.”.

Hibs chief executive Dan Barnett added: “The inclusion of Easter Road as a Candidate Stadium for the 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup is fantastic news for the Club and the City of Edinburgh.

"This is something we've been working hard on for several months, with various positive discussions with the Scottish FA and key stakeholders. In recent years, we have been delighted to host Scotland Women's National Team matches at Easter Road, so to be named as a Candidate Stadium for the finals in 2035 is a huge honour.

In a recent development, “To have the opportunity to showcase our stadium on the world's biggest stage would be an immensely proud moment for the Club. It presents a unique opportunity to welcome tens of thousands of supporters from across the world to Edinburgh and create a lasting legacy for the women's game.

"We're excited by the next steps and the prospect of working alongside the Scottish FA, the City of Edinburgh Council and our partners to help bring this opportunity to life.”.

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold. FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

The tournament will feature 48 nations and 104 matches across 39 days, with the final host cities and stadiums to be confirmed by FIFA in due course.

The team had to settle for a point after Rovers striker Matty Fanimo hit a stunner to bring the scores level at 2-2.

In isolation a point on the road is perfectly acceptable, but Mansell was feeling the effect of six league games without a win – and now 15 games without a win on grass.

His team are quietly working their way down the table, occupying 15th place.

Industry observers note that buoyed by the permanent signing of winger George Vorster Hill played very well for 30 second-half minutes. Vorster put the visitors 2-1 in front on 75 minutes but then Hill seemed to go defensive and gave away a cheap free kick 25 yards out. Up stepped Fanimo to break away hearts.

Perhaps the more stinging result was a 1-0 home defeat to lowly Brentwood the previous Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that mansell and his team held all the aces that night but for some reason couldn’t break out from a malaise. They produced one shot on target all evening. The winning goal was a very scrappy affair ending with three Hillian defenders on their backsides as Alfie Cerulli bundled home from a yard.

Mansell was quite direct in his post-match interview after that loss, saying: “Gutted, it’s a familiar pill to swallow, there wasn’t enough desire in both boxes.”.

There were raised blood pressures among fan walking away from the MTC that evening and a mixed bag of social media comments.

Away from first team matters we caught up junior section managers Tim Bourne and Ben Slade, who are passionate about providing a safe and nurturing environment for youngsters to play football.

As Tim explained: “We have over 500 players both training and playing matches across our three home facilities.”.

The MTC is a hive of activity on Saturday mornings for training and then the excellent new facility The Arc and St Paul’s School host matches on Sundays.

Ben stated: “it’s a huge operation and while Tim and I are the face, there is a large committee of passionate people all performing different tasks, this wouldn’t function without them!.”.

According to recent reports, hill’s Junior section has three teams at each age group, the youngest players are under-fives. They also facilitate coaching badges and referee courses. As Tim suggested: “It’s a well-oiled machine.”.

I ventured to the Arc last Sunday to catch up with the U13s girls team playing Fishersgate. It truly is a remarkable facility, a real mecca for youth football. Both teams put on a great performance as the visitors took a narrow victory.

The junior section is in rude health and going from strength to strength operating with the best facilities in Sussex.

Hill’s pathway section under Mansell and Berty Oliva are performing at an extraordinary level this season – the U18s and 19s Academy side continue to pick up great wins.

Striker Bobby Byrne – son of ex-Republic of Ireland, Brighton and QPR striker John Byrne – and is making all kinds of headlines after his nine goals in one U18 Sussex Cup match. He swiftly followed up with six for the U19s at Ebbsfleet.

According to recent reports, after the six he explained: “It’s all going very well this season. I would like to take my football to the highest level I can but first would love to play for the Hillians.”.

Bobby’s name is on a lot of people’s lips right now – with many calling for him to make his first team debut. It’s a certainty we will be keeping an eye on his progress.

While the club are operating at a high level right now and are always looking to enhance the profile, the vast majority of fans and connections quite rightly engage only with first team matters.

Recent findings suggest that mansell is acutely aware of this so will be looking for a win when title contenders Eastbourne Borough travel to the MTC on Saturday afternoon. Three points at this time would be huge.

Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea Hibs players do not enjoying playing at home as they bid to halt a 10-game run without victory at Easter Road in the William Hill Premiership.

The Hibees have not won a league game on their own turf since defeating Kilmarnock 3-0 in early April and their supporters turned on them during a grim 4-0 defeat by Dundee United on Saturday that left them second bottom of the table.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

If they fail to beat Dundee on Tuesday, the winless streak in Leith will extend beyond the eight-month mark.

“I don’t know,” stated midfielder McGrath on why he thought they were struggling for results at Easter Road. “Personally, I always like playing at home. I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a significant open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

“It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb. It’s hard to put your finger on it, but it’s something that we’re trying to put right.”.

After a difficult start to the season which resulted in Marink Reedijk replacing David Gray as manager in late September, it looked like Hibs had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

In a recent development, mcGrath, therefore, is hopeful Saturday’s aberration will prove a blip. “We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us,” noted the Republic of Ireland international. Or not a tricky time, but we were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams.

“It’s frustrating not to build on that, but hopefully we can put Saturday down to a bad day and get back on track.”.

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs being 11th in the table as he senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

“It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute,” he remarked. “It’s obviously not where we want to be.

Industry observers note that “We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial in terms of there being nine points in the next week up for grabs. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.

“It’s just about finding that consistency to hopefully propel us up the league.”.

Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2086 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • Recent findings suggest that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

Recent findings suggest that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

Industry observers note that the charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Sources indicate that each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

There has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

Industry observers note that however, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is said to be one of the most serious of the 115.

Industry observers note that the damning verdict for City is a major new test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

Sources indicate that the Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

City have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are remarked to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

It has been revealed that city rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for new players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

On Friday, a City spokesman said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and declared in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

According to recent reports, city denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

It did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, remarked: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

“Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

Ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, said the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, mentioned he believed the club were innocent.

“For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder remarked while on international duty.

“When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, said: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of Fresh York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 said that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

All the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

They can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

According to recent reports, the next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

Industry observers note that as well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

Recent findings suggest that A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

According to recent reports, we also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

According to recent reports, city have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they said that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

At the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also remarked: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

Sources indicate that of the Football Leaks documents, City said: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:36.
  • Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri will reunite with his parent club when Borussia Dortmund take on the Premier League champions in Tuesday's Champions League clash at the Emirates Stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:36.

Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri will reunite with his parent club when Borussia Dortmund take on the Premier League champions in Tuesday's Champions League clash at the Emirates Stadium.

The 19-year-old joined the German giants on a season-long loan during the final hours of the summer transfer window, but he is yet to find his best form under Niko Kovac.

Nwaneri has only provided one assist and no goals from his first 13 appearances in a Dortmund shirt across all competitions, that contribution coming on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim.

Since then, the 2007-born playmaker has only started four Bundesliga matches, and he is still waiting to make a first XI in the Champions League, being restricted to 87 minutes across four substitute outings.

Nwaneri was also given just a one-minute run-out in the weekend's 1-0 Bundesliga win over Borussia Monchengladbach, but he may be given the chance to strut his stuff against his boyhood team.

Champions League rules permit loan players to face their parent clubs in the Champions League, so Nwaneri will be able to feature in Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Unlike in the Premier League and other domestic competitions in England, where loan players cannot take on parent teams without special dispensation, there are no such restrictions outlined in the Champions League rules and regulations.

However, if Nwaneri was to return to Arsenal in January, the England Under-21 international would not be able to feature for the Premier League champions for the remainder of the tournament.

Article 30.05 of UEFA's Champions League regulations states that 'A player may not play in the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League or UEFA Conference League for more than one club in a single season', but Arsenal are not expected to bring Nwaneri back to North London over the winter.

The teenager has scored 10 goals and set up two more in 51 Arsenal games since making his debut against Brentford in September 2022, when he became the Premier League's youngest player of all time.

Goal Bayern Munich. Philippe Coutinho. 2-8.

Loan players making decisive contributions against parent clubs in the Champions League has been a semi-regular occurrence, the most notable example being Philippe Coutinho in 2020.

The then-Barcelona playmaker was shipped out to Bayern Munich and reunited with La Blaugrana in the quarter-finals of the 2019-20 edition, when he incredibly scored twice in an 8-2 annihilation.

Sixteen years prior, Fernando Morientes - on loan at Monaco from Real Madrid - scored in both legs of the quarter-final against Los Blancos, helping Les Monegasques knock out his parent team on away goals before they lost to Porto in the final.

It has been revealed that real were also stung by James Rodriguez in the 2017-18 semi-finals vs. Bayern Munich, but the Colombian's goal - which he refused to celebrate - was not enough to prevent Los Blancos advancing 4-3 on aggregate.

The 2013-14 semi-finals saw Thibaut Courtois play a crucial role in Atletico Madrid's success against parent club Chelsea, who tried to force Los Rojiblancos to pay them £2.5m for each game the Belgian goalkeeper played against them, only for UEFA to rule the terms null, void and unenforceable.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that news of upcoming contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 19 November 2026.

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer. Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s new four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

Sources indicate that news of upcoming contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours. Extending players when they're approaching the final two years of their contract isn't revolutionary, but the spate of them in such quick succession drew the eye.

Most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s fresh contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on latest contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year.

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree new terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month.

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

He told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’.

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

In a recent development, now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The proposal to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

According to recent reports, the biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

In a recent development, the injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

Kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next big decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

It has been revealed that havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain crucial to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

Mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

Given most of the players who have agreed latest long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Significant Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

Recent findings suggest that the environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be mentioned for stars at every club in the league.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

When Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his fresh midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager said: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’.

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement.

It has been revealed that the collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that this season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

In a recent development, much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

He has spoken to Sussexworld and the Eastbourne Herald about the decision – and outlined some of the difficulties they had faced with injury and unavailability this season in a run of results that ironically had recently looked like it might be coming to an end.

Town confirmed Macdonald’s departure on Saturday in a statement and have since installed club stalwart Dave Winterton as interim manager and asked fans to get behind him.

Macdonald stated of his sacking: “It was a surprise to be honest and there was absolutely zero warning, which you often anticipate with this sort of thing.

"I spoke to the chairman eight days earlier (the day before the Sheppey game) and he told me on that call that my role was “bomb-proof” and that I had his backing.

"I had explained to him in the call how hard it had been this season, but we didn’t have a relationship where we talked regularly on the phone so we hadn’t had an opportunity to discuss things previously.

"On Saturday, the chairman told one of my assistants at the final whistle to tell me to come to the office. It was the first league game that the chairman had attended since August so I obviously didn’t think too much of it, but that was when he delivered the news to me around 20 minutes after the game had finished.

"He did it along with another member of staff who I’ve never been introduced to before, but is also apparently a committee member.

"The chairman told me my position was being ended at the club and noted that they thought it would be better to announce it as a resignation, which I rejected.

Recent findings suggest that "I wasn’t given a reason, despite asking for one multiple times. The chairman just kept shrugging and it wasn’t his fault it was just what the board wanted. I was told that the board held a vote on the previous Monday (November 16) and the decision was made, which is when they made a call to another manager on speaker to offer the job/sound out his interest. The likely new manager told me this on Saturday evening.

"The club then let me manage the Lewes game on the Tuesday, take training Thursday, sign two players on Friday and manage Saturday’s game without anybody saying anything to me, despite knowing they were going to sack me after the Saturday game.".

It has been revealed that it is Macdonald and one of his right-hand men, Ben Davis, who have been sacked. Macdonald remarked: “The club wanted my other two assistants, Matthew Elphick and Adam Davidson, to remain in position, but they have rejected that opportunity.”.

Macdonald outlined some of the difficulties Town have faced this season which have left them struggling, having won just two league games to sit second from bottom of the Isthmian SE table after 19 games.

According to recent reports, he told us: “It has been no secret that we have been completely decimated by injuries through the season and have only once played the same XI two games running. We had started to get bodies in the door and back on the pitch.

"We’d drawn our last two games and arguably could have won both, so it is frustrating that the club made the call they did when the tide was clearly turning.”.

Macdonald outlined the injuries the squad had faced: Oliver Davies - ruptured PCL; Anesu Sismayi - Head injury; Marcin Ruda - fractured foot; JJ Walker - hip flexor & suspension; Leon Greig - knee injury (3 months missed); Luke Emberson - shin splints & groin; Aussie Pugh - ankle & knee; Aaron Capon - hamstring & back; Jack Murphy - heel & suspension; Sonny Walsh - jaw; Eliot Jenks - hamstring; Oli Deda - concussion (missed 3 games); Reuel Powell-Downey - hamstring; Arron Hopkinson - suspension.

He added: “That is a fraction of the list.”.

Looking back at his time as Town boss, Macdonald talked about some of those who had helped him and his staff: “Since we’ve been at the club, David Jenkins has been absolutely incredible. The work he does for the club, the selflessness and support he gives it is truly unbelievable. He is what non-league is about. Anything we needed, he always did his best to help us with.

"Ross Perrin this season has also been a huge help to us and supported us throughout, as have Luci Del-Gaudio and Paul Lewis. Josh Claxton and Ed have both been incredible. What Josh has done with the social media and all other online stuff is just amazing and he done so much for the club that never got noticed. Josh has also left the football club.

In a recent development, "Former 23s and 18s managers Shaun Lee, Giuseppe Lombardelli and Ryan Reid were always a huge help and incredibly supportive. There are dozens of others that have backed and supported us throughout our time like Ken Wilkins and Chris Prior. Truly great people.

Sources indicate that "A huge thank you to all the players over the years. They have done so much for us and we really appreciate all their efforts.

In a recent development, "The biggest thank you is to our management team and support staff, who have just been incredible throughout our time together at the club. Ben Davis, Matt Elphick, Adam Davidson, David Winterton, Roman Glazier and Dom Crowhurst have all made my Saturdays so enjoyable. They’ve all worked so hard for the players and deserve huge credit.”.

Sources indicate that macdonald is in no hurry to find a new non-league job: “I would expect to relax and have a break from it all to be honest. I will try to take in other games and training sessions with other managers wherever I can. I’m trying not to think too much about what comes next because you can’t predict anything in non-league.”.

He added: “You don’t often get the chance to manage the club from the town you grew up in and I’ve just committed over 10% of my life to it, so the next few days and weeks will just be reflecting on that and appreciating the opportunity that the club gave me four-and-a-half years ago, and the continued and consistent success we have given them in return.”.

We have asked Eastbourne Town if anyone wishes to respond to any of Macdonald’s comments.

However, Blackburn remain with just one away win this campaign, only recording seven points from eight matches while shipping 15 goals.

Without a win in 10 league games since September 2 and in their worst league position for many a year, the Oakwell outfit look like being in the thick of a survival fight for the rest of the season and face the very real prospect of fourth-tier football next term for the first time since 1978-79 if their fortunes don't turn around in the new year.

It's a far cry from their highs in their one season under Duff in 2022-23 when they reached the play-off final and went desperately close to promotion back to the Championship.

Duff, who was at Oakwell to watch his old club take on Sheffield Wednesday on Friday - the hosts lost 2-1, the margin of defeat for their past five league losses - remarked: "Barnsley didn't look like a wounded animal on Friday, but a football team with loads of energy and good players.

"I don't think we're at a point now where we can assume that, well: 'we're just better than them'. Everything that's got us, this football club, the team, the squad, to where it has and the success it's had, is because it's had that underdog mentality. What we can't have is we slip into 'oh, we're better than them'.. Because that's when trouble starts, isn't it?

"I watched them on Friday against Sheffield Wednesday and they should have got some out of the game.

"Barnsley found themselves 2-0 down and then were really, really good for the rest of the game.

It has been revealed that "It's not like the Premier League where you very rarely see teams at the bottom of the league beat the teams at the top. In this league, it happens all the time.

“Bromley have beaten Reading, Peterborough have beaten Plymouth. It's not a league where you (think) we’ll beat them or ‘two home games, we’ll win them’.

Recent findings suggest that "Our lads' mentality and attitude is pretty good. I don't think we have that sort of arrogance in terms of ‘we'll be alright, we'll just win today.’.

"They know what they have to do, they know the effort they have to put in, the application, the energy they have to put into every game and since I've been here they've done that every game.

"They did it before we came and, like I stated, they just nicked a couple early in the season. We've done enough where we should have won them and we haven't quite nicked them.".

City are on a run of nine matches in just under a month in four different competitions and they face midweek games for the next four matches. Tonight is also their final game of a six-match run of fixtures at Valley Parade.

Duff continued: "There are games that are coming now.

"There’s no way there is going to be the same 11 players on Tuesday or the following Saturday or the following Tuesday or the following Saturday.

"We’ll wrap a few up that we need to and there will be opportunities for people.

Industry observers note that "The good thing with competition is they know they’ll get opportunities so they need to be ready. If you get given a chance and you don’t take it, it might not come around again so rapidly.

"That’s when the training of the lads who aren’t in the team is so important, the lifestyle, the commitment to the job, the commitment to the team.

It has been revealed that "Don’t be the one that’s caught out partying or eating junk food because you’re not letting yourself down, you’re letting your teammates down. But I don’t think we need to worry about any of that in this group.".

The victory saw Broadbridge Heath move into one of the play-off places in seventh – just one point behind Hastings United.

Fixtures continue to come thick and fast with the Bears travelling to second-placed Erith Town on Tuesday evening before returning home again on Saturday to face leaders Faversham Town.

  • An old adage is that it’s best to go again as promptly as possible to get the performance and - most urgently of all – the result out of the system.
