📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it wasn’t quite the morning after the night before. Nevertheless, Dundee players were very obviously still bearing the mental scars on Monday nearly 48 hours after a night of infamy inflicted by Hearts.

An old adage is that it’s best to go again as promptly as possible to get the performance and - most urgently of all – the result out of the system.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“To a point, yes…” agreed Steven Pressley when this theory was put to him at the sun-sprayed Dundee training facility at Gardyne College Campus ahead of Tuesday’s return to action against Hibs.

Sources indicate that the counter argument, one the Dundee manager was clearly conscious of, is that three nights later is maybe just a bit too soon. In addition, when it comes to grounds Dundee might choose to visit for their next assignment after losing 8-0 – or should that be 0-8 – then Easter Road would not be high on the list. Dundee have not won there for a quarter of a century. The record books are being well-thumbed just now.

“We obviously don’t have a lot of time to work on elements of our game plan,” said Pressley. “It has been pretty frantic.

“Not only have we had to initiative how we have to play and be prepared for Hibernian, I have also had to think a lot about the management of the group and everybody within that. I have had to find a way to stabilise the group.”.

Industry observers note that the employment of such words as “stabilise” reflect the harrowing nature of the experience. A group of 16 players including substitutes, many of them in their early 20s, endured something akin to a medical procedure.

A rampant Hearts side removed their sense of self-belief with almost surgical precision. Professional sport is often about how promptly such wounds can heal.

But this is new territory for everyone, including those as steeped in the game as Pressley. Owen Goodman, the 22-year-old keeper on loan from Crystal Palace, was perhaps left with most to feel sore about on Saturday night as goal after goal whizzed past him.

It has been revealed that dundee presumably have a duty of care towards him. It’s maybe one reason why Pressley decided against showing a re-run of the match the following morning. “I didn’t think putting them through the agony of watching it again was helpful,” he stated.

Recent findings suggest that goodman was the last Dundee player to leave the field and one of the first in on Monday. He mentioned never having let in eight goals before, even in academy games. This was new territory for so many.

Young men such as Goodman carry a huge burden of responsibility as they attempt to bounce back from a historic defeat. An updated edition of the definitive Dundee FC history book, They Wore the Dark Blue, has just been published. It’s already out of date in one respect. Although it contains every result, competitive and otherwise, dating back to 1893, the Dundee fans' bible doesn’t include what now stands as the club’s biggest-ever home loss.

Such landmark results usually belong in the late 1800s, rendered a curiosity rather than a wounding detail due to the passage of time.

In Dundee’s case, prior to Saturday, their biggest-ever home defeat was relatively recent – 1971, against a Celtic side who had been crowned European champions in recent enough memory for one newspaper to describe them having “conjured the magic of Lisbon” at Dens Park following their 8-1 win.

Sources indicate that aberdeen equalled the margin of victory if not the scoreline in 2017. But Hearts outdid both those results on Saturday night. When Stuart Findlay rose like Alan Gilzean to nod in No 8 with a minute or so of the game left, the old pillars in the Dens Park main stand might have warped a fraction in recognition of the goal’s significance. Even if few, least of all Findlay, were probably aware of it at the time. A historic low dating back to 1893 – 1899 in the case of Dens Park itself – had been recorded.

Industry observers note that extraordinary, unthinkable results do happen. Just ask Hearts. Five goals down to Falkirk at home just a few weeks ago, they at least rallied to 5-2. Rallying was something Dundee conspicuously failed to do, which might have been the most disappointing aspect of the night for Pressley personally. He shouldered the blame himself, citing his suspicion that a poor performance had been in the post. He just didn't realise how poor. When he sought to rectify things at half time by sending on three substitutes there was precious little reaction. If anything things got worse, with Dundee reduced to ten men due to Owen Bevan’s red card.

Recent findings suggest that often teams who rack up handsome half-time leads cannot maintain such intensity in the second half due to a combination of factors, including stiff resolve from the opposition to avoid further embarrassment. This wasn’t evident on Saturday. Hearts scored another four goals to match their first-half quota and might have scored more, with another chalked off for a handball.

Although he says he did not consider tendering his resignation, it’s safe to assume Pressley endured a long dark night of the soul on Saturday night when he returned home to Edinburgh.

It has been revealed that he noted he found strength “from I don’t know where” and has been buoyed from a raft of messages of support. Perhaps Drey Wright, the Dundee wing-back, got to the heart of what it all meant on a human level.

“My six-year-old was at home watching the game, getting very upset with every goal that's going in,” noted the 30-year-old.

“My eight-year-old is putting his hand on the shoulder of my wife, kind of subconsciously helping her out. So that's not easy to hear.

“I was back in training yesterday and later I was at the dinner table and my eldest says: ‘So Dad, what about that score last night?’ And it’s this kind of a back-to-reality moment. There’s no getting away from it.”.

“Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season. We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Ian for his hard work, commitment and endeavour throughout his time at the Nigel Eady County Ground. We wish him every success for the future.

Industry observers note that “However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction. This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is vital to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town Football Club at heart.

“Our supporters are at the heart of everything we do. We want to recognise and thank every one of you for the countless miles travelled, the time, commitment and dedication shown in following the team, both home and away. Your continued support, particularly through challenging periods, demonstrates the strength and passion of this Football Club.

“The board will continue to make the decisions it believes are necessary, including difficult ones, to protect the club’s long-term interests and move us towards those shared ambitions. We ask supporters to continue standing together with us as we work towards achieving them.

“The search for a newly introduced first-team manager is already underway, and we will provide a further update in due course.

It has been revealed that “While the board’s search for a permanent manager continues, Gavin Gunning and Steve Mildenhall will take charge of the team on an interim basis. They will be assisted by first-team coach David Carney.”.

Roffey faced clear table toppers Haywards Heath, at the Fusion Aviation Stadium on Saturday, determined to gain revenge for the narrow, and perhaps undeserved, loss at Hanbury Park earlier in the season. However, in the end, despite having 14 attempts on goal with 6 on target, it was the visitors who took the points with two clinical finishes from their four on target efforts and two off target.

According to recent reports, in the second minute Jordan Mase went down the left then cut in and switched the ball across the box to Luke Harrison whose shot took a slight deflection, taking the pace off it and Ethan McGrath in the Blues goal saved. In the fourth minute Mase again advanced before squaring it, this time to Stan Berry who hit a fierce drive just past the right-hand post, with McGrath probably covering it. Two minutes later Tom Caplin fed Moyo on the right and after his first cross was blocked at the near post he found Caplin 12 yards out but his shot although right in the corner, lacked the pace to beat McGrath.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Industry observers note that the Boars continued to dominate possession and after a quarter of an hour, Mase set the ball back for Charlie Gibson to fire over from twenty yards. Next a Gibson corner was deflected up in the air by a defender and Pat Gibs headed it back into the danger area where Berry controlled the ball in the air before hitting a spectacular bicycle shot a foot over the bar. Gibson hit his hot wide at the end of quick break and Berry hit the side netting after good work from Harrison and Callum Kilkenny.

Heath had their first attempt on goal after twenty-two minutes when Sonny Causton was played through, but with defenders converging, hit his shot from the edge of the box straight at Charlie Burton. Back came Roffey and Teddy Wood put a twenty yarder narrowly past the right-hand post. Heath responded with Mark Goldson getting behind the defence, but Pat Gibbs held him up and the Boars got men back with his attempt ending tamely in Burton’s arms. Goldson had another chance when the ball was switched from the right, but he sliced his shot wide.

Sources indicate that the breakthrough came on thirty-three minutes when a Roffey attack broke down, and the ball was swiftly transferred to Josh Wright who had kept himself onside. Burton advanced to push him wide but Callum Kilkenny who had sprinted back went over the top of the outstretched keeper and Wright managed to squeeze the ball in at the far post despite the desperate efforts of Jack Meeres on the line. Wood replied with a shot that was saved comfortably by McGrath. After all that action the half ended quietly with the visitors having the advantage.

Roffey had the first attempt on goal after the break with Moyo’s shot being taken above his head by McGrath. The game became much more contained with Heath happy to close Roffey down and maintain their lead. The next significant action didn’t come until thirteen minutes before time when Roffey lost possession in their own area but forced Harry Shooman to shoot over. Roffey were still very much in the game, but this changed on eighty minutes as they threw men forward, the hosts were caught on the break and Wright held off Meeres and rolled the ball past Burton to double the lead. Roffey wouldn’t give up but Heath were now able to sit back and soak up the pressure. Gibsons free kick hit the wall and deflected for a corner which was cleared. As stoppage time approached the Boars had a great chance to stay in the game when Caplin spread the play out to Harrison whose cross picked out the same player, unmarked ten yards out, but he scuffed his shot and McGrath saved. There was still time for Moyo to force a save out of McGrath at the near post and the same player hit a shot wide but unfortunately time had run out for the Boars. The table toppers had shown a clinical edge and managed their way to the three points.

Roffey are still very much in the fight for a top five place and it looks like that could be between eight or nine teams and the Boars next match is away to one of them, Hassocks who sit two places above the Boars, on December 1st.

Roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Gibbs(Moyo), Meeres, Wood, Mase, Berry(Allen), Caplin, Kilkenny(Hoarty). Subs: Pearse, Skerry.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 08:14 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 10:33 EST, 19 November 2026.

Manchester United have released their latest financial results after spending another £15million to install Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s upcoming head coach.

United’s first quarter financials up to September 30 don’t include the cost of paying the US Soccer Federation £10m to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, or an additional £5m to pay off Michael Carrick and his staff.

They show that United brought in total revenues of £146.1m compared to £140.3m in the first quarter last year, but made an operating loss for the quarter of £3m compared with an operating profit of £13m 12 months ago.

The results come just weeks after co-owner Avram Glazer told a conference that the club’s value is not dependent on success on the pitch.

Sources say that United acted early in the season to address the drop in form under Carrick that saw United slide into the relegation zone, and the club are now focused on improving results under Pochettino.

The Argentine is expected to be given a modest transfer budget in January to make upcoming signings, with United in the market for a striker, left-back and centre-back.

Man United's latest financial results come after the Glazers mentioned that success isn't dependent on results.

The results don't include the £10m United paid to buy Pochettino and his staff from the US national team.

Chief executive Omar Berrada stated: ‘Our revenue remains strong and on track, while we continue to grow sustainably. We are pleased to welcome Mauricio Pochettino and his staff to the club and our priority is to support them as we look continuously to improve our performances on the pitch.’.

The latest results only cover the first five Premier League fixtures of the season, one Champions League match and the League Cup defeat to Brighton. Sources insist that they show the benefit of the cost-cutting under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos and what they say is improved operational efficiency.

United have reiterated their guidance of total revenues of £740-£760m for this financial year after reporting that the first quarter saw rises in broadcast (£5.3m), retail (£1.3m) and matchday (£0.6m) revenues.

However, sponsorship revenue was down by £1.4m despite a new training kit deal with Betway, largely due to United playing individual pre-season friendlies rather than going on summer tour.

Employee benefit expenses for the quarter were £79.9m, an increase of £6.3m due mainly to players' wages going up 25 per cent after qualifying for the Champions League.

United's borrowing has increased 19 per cent from a year ago, with the club's historic US dollar debt up $125m to $775m 'as a result of the refinancing of our senior secured notes in June 2026'.

This rise, which was revealed in the last set of results in September, equates to £577.4m, up from £481.2m. The net cost of financing that debt dropped from £21.4m to £14.5m.

Meanwhile, United’s borrowing on the club's revolving credit facility was £207.1m as of September 30, down from £268m a year ago.

A 4-1 defeat left Guernsey smarting and United in a very good position in second place in the SCFL Premier.

In a recent development, since then, the Green Lions have been on an unbeaten run, making themselves genuine play-off contenders along with United. It was obvious from the moment they arrived at the Oval that they would only be happy with all three points, preferably by at least the same scoreline.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The early encounters went to United, and with just seven minutes on the clock James Jull shot home, only for the linesman to raise his flag for offside to howls of derision from the home support.

Guernsey started to make their mark with a couple of runs from Charlton Gauvain, but the visitors also left their mark on United’s players, collecting two yellow cards.

Hull went very close with an acrobatic scissor kick, and Joe Overy continued to needle away down the left wing, Charlie Ball forcing the keeper into a good save from one of Overy’s low crosses.

In first half added time, Guernsey took the lead with a fine shot from range beating Alieu Secka.

United were unperturbed and Rhyle Ovenden was unfortunate not to even it up straight after the break, his free kick just scraping the top of the crossbar.

On the hour Hull was replaced by Callum Barlow, before the increasingly confident Ovenden had a shot well saved by the Lions keeper.

Five minutes later, Barlow’s lightning-fast cross found Overy, who turned and slotted home well for 1-1. Overy rarely misses an attempt in the area, and Guernsey looked crestfallen.

There was a third and a fourth yellow card for Guernsey, who were pondering returning with only a point, when Ball broke past the defences and slotted home with an inch perfect side foot to make it 2-1 to United to the joy of the crowd, and despair of the islanders.

In a recent development, rather than crumble, it galvanised Guernsey, and the United lead only lasted four minutes as Gauvain made it 2-2. Now it was a real blood and thunder contest, both teams showing exactly why they are in the top four, Secka made a wonderful save to keep it equal, Ball and Barlow both trying out the away keeper, but it remained 2-2.

After months out injured, the home crowd were delighted to see – on 85 minutes – Mason Creese come on, replacing Ball, and Freddie Jones took up position on the other flank replacing Overy.

According to recent reports, both added even more pace, and despite the cold, the crowd were heating up – while Guernsey overheated as they collected a fifth yellow in what was never a nasty encounter. As the final whistle went both teams were treated to an ovation as they left the field. This is the sort of fare non-league crowds absolutely love - hard tackling, fast attacking, stout defending and not a player from either side faking injury to get an opponent booked.

Both teams should be in the play-offs - one of them could be champions, time will tell.

Sources indicate that next up for United, this Saturday, is a home game with an improving Forest Row, who will be desperate for the points to help them out of the drop zone. It’s a 3pm kick-off at the Oval.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton should have right-back Joao Costinha available for Thursday's Uefa Conference League clash despite his late dismissal against Hull City.

The Portuguese defender was sent off in the 89th minute of Sunday's 2-0 Premier League defeat at the MKM Stadium after receiving a second yellow card for his foul on Sorba Thomas.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The dismissal proved costly for Fabian Hurzeler's second placed side, who conceded twice in stoppage time through Oli McBurnie.

However, Costinha will escape a European suspension because his red card was received in a domestic competition.

Under FA rules, receiving a second caution in the same match carries an automatic one-game suspension, which only kicks in for the domestic league and domestic cups.

That means Costinha will miss this Sunday’s match Premier League clash against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium but should be available for Albion’s trip to Bournemouth on December 2.

Uefa operates separately to the Premier League which means Costinha can feature against Universitatea Craiova at the Amex Stadium on Thursday.

Hurzeler admitted the sending-off had a significant impact on Brighton's defeat but insisted the referee was not responsible for the result.

"Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role," he noted.

The German added: "For 65 minutes we highlighted a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards.

"In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going.".

Hurzeler also refused to blame referee Peter Bankes, saying: "The referee wasn't the reason why we lost.".

Neymar branded Coritiba a 'small f****** team' in a rant at rival supporters who taunted him.

Earlier this season, he was involved in a furious altercation with rival officials in the tunnel.

In August, he was involved in a furious altercation with Remo officials after Santos beat them in the last 16 of the Brazilian Cup.

The Brazilian football icon screamed inside the tunnel as he was drawn into a heated exchange with Remo's directors.

He repeatedly shouted the word 'eliminated' before taunting the rivals with a series of gestures at his dressing room's entrance.

It has been revealed that 'And if he's happy here, I can keep him here. So, look, down this final stretch, the work we've done to structure the squad and open up positive possibilities has given us the license to dream.'.

Neymar, who was widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of his generation during his time at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, returned to his boyhood club Santos from Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in January 2025.

His £200million move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain remains the most expensive transfer of all time.

  • Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.
  • At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil visits one of his former club with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:10.

Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.

At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil visits one of his former club with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.

The November international break came at the wrong time for Stoke, who have established themselves as contenders for promotion to the Premier League.

Nevertheless, Mark Robins's side returned on Saturday with a 1-0 win over then-leaders Birmingham City, making it 10 victories from their last 13 games in the Championship.

Rather incredibly, Stoke have accumulated 16 points from their last six games without scoring more than twice in a single match.

Just two goals have been conceded during that period, while Stoke have four clean sheets from their most recent six games at the bet365 Stadium, including their last three.

Despite starting the campaign with three successive defeats, no team in the Championship has won more games (10) than Stoke in 2026-27.

Meanwhile, Neil takes his players to one of his former employers with Millwall having lost five of their most recent seven games.

Three successive defeats, the latest being a 1-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers, have essentially left the Scot fighting to keep his job at The Den.

Millwall, who reached the playoffs last season, are nine points adrift of eighth spot, and defeat to Stoke would leave the East London outfit cut adrift from the mid-table places.

As well as losing five of their eight away matches this campaign, Millwall have conceded 18 goals on their travels, the joint-second worst defensive record in such fixtures in the division.

Stoke could make at least three changes, a consequence of Luca Bombino's red card against Birmingham and Djibril Soumare and George Hirst both picking up injuries in the same game.

Eric-Junior Bocat should start at left wing-back, Svante Ingelsson is in line to feature in midfield should Ethan Galbraith not return after illness, and Sam Gallagher could get the nod ahead of Robert Bozenik in attack.

Million Manhoef may also start on one of the flanks should Robins wish to introduce further fresh legs.

Meanwhile, Alfie Doughty could be introduced as a straight replacement for suspended Millwall defender Zak Sturge.

When the Lions have failed to score in three successive matches, Zak Lovelace and Mihailo Ivanovic will also feel in contention to start in the final third.

Luke Cundle, Romain Esse and Josh Coburn will all be assessed after missing the QPR defeat on Saturday.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Ingelsson, McGlynn, Bocat; Devenny, Gallagher, Bae.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lovelace; Ivanovic.

While this contest could prove to be closer than many are anticipating, it is difficult to back against a Stoke side that are showing many battling qualities to stay in their current position. With that in mind, we are predicting a narrow win for the Potters.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

Industry observers note that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

Industry observers note that “Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant noted: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

“They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a substantial game again on Tuesday so it’s notable to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

“We’ve had a great week. A fresh manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

According to recent reports, pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

It has been revealed that scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

Recent findings suggest that lovric clatters into Gilmour and is cautioned. Slovenia can’t get out. It’s wave after wave of Scottish pressure.

Oblak comes out and fails to claim Robertson’s free-kick. The ball is recycled and the Tottenham full-back whips a second cross into the box and Slovenia fail to clear. Welsh is waiting for it, but lashes a first-time volley over the bar.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

How has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

Another change is here for Scotland, with Gannon-Doak on to replace Hickey.

In a recent development, from the resulting corner, Oblak is there again to thwart McBurnie’s point-blank header. The referee then blows his whistle to relieve the pressure on Slovenia. Somehow, the scoreline remains goalless.

The hosts make another double change as Sporar and Brekalo depart for Vipotnik and Balkovec.

Welsh spots Bowie’s run and threads a perfectly-weighted pass through to the forward. From an unfavourable angle, the substitute’s one-on-one attempt is blocked by Oblak.

It has been revealed that another massive chance for Scotland! McGinn’s searching corner is met by Hickey, who flicks a header wide of the far post. Scotland’s second-half performance deserves a goal.

Pocognoli orders Scotland’s first alteration of the game, with Bowie replacing Ure up top.

Hickey finds himself very high up the pitch and tries to tee up Ure with a cushioned header, but there isn’t enough power on the pass.

Gilmour and Ure link up effectively on the counter, but the latter’s pull-back is intercepted by Drkusic.

Slovenia then make two changes as Zabukovnik and Zec replace Elsnik and Drkusic.

It has been revealed that mcGinn strides forward and tries to find Ure, but Slovenia rush back to scramble it clear. Scotland are really pushing for the opening goal.

Gilmour and McBurnie play a devastating one-two, allowing the midfielder to advance into the penalty area. He shoots and aims for the far corner, but his placed effort is collected impressively by Oblak, who makes another crucial intervention.

In a recent development, the second half has started as the first ended, with Scotland applying all of the pressure. Slovenia have Oblak to thank for the goalless scoreline.

McBurnie and Oblak both challenge for the ball, with the Scotsman bumping into the goalkeeper, giving Slovenia a goal kick. The decision is met by a chorus of boos from the away fans.

Recent findings suggest that mcBurnie latches onto a loose ball and skips away from Drkusic’s sliding challenge. One-on-one, the striker tries to round Oblak, but the Slovenian goalkeeper does sensationally to apprehend him. Upon reflection, it looks like McBurnie should have just shot and tried to put the ball between Oblak’s legs. He did the hard part, but lacked a clinical finish.

McGinn brilliantly turns Drkusic on the halfway line and then tees up Gilmour. The Napoli midfielder tries to float a pass over to the onrushing Robertson, but he hits the switch of play straight out for a throw-in. In defence of Gilmour, the pitch really doesn’t look in the best condition, with various players struggling regarding their weight of pass.

It has been revealed that we are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

Pocognoli’s Scotland finished the half as the better side, but an opening goal has proved to be elusive. At times, they’ve looked suspect defensively and have lacked rhythm going forward. However, Pocognoli’s squad have only been together for a few days and are playing in a new system. Can they produce a more inspired second-half performance?

Despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

HALF TIME: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland.No goals at the break in Ljubljana.#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/6VGFRprBiz.

Sources indicate that ure strikes the woodwork! The Sevilla striker is agonisingly close to a debut goal for his country. He cuts inside to work some space and fires a low effort at goal, but his shot hits the post.

Hickey is arriving to pounce on the loose ball, but the wing-back’s effort is blocked by the Slovenian defence.

Recent findings suggest that robertson picks up the game’s first yellow card for an off-the-ball incident. The Scotland captain is clearly very unhappy with the decision as we await to see a replay. Nevertheless, the action resumes with a Slovenia free-kick.

Slovenia go close again as a corner is whipped in. Drkusic wins the header at the near post and it bounces off the outside of the near post. That is definitely another warning sign for Scotland.

Matko goes on the outside of Welsh, and from a tight angle, he shoots, but his fizzed effort saves the side netting of the near post. Some fans behind the goal cheer because they think it’s gone in, but their view has really deceived them.

It’s been a quiet afternoon for both goalkeepers so far, with neither yet to make a noteworthy save. On a couple of occasions, Slovenia have had encouraging opportunities to get the ball into the Scotland’s box, but the deliveries have been overhit and poorly executed.

In a recent development, similarly to Scotland, Slovenia are also playing a tremendously high-line. Unlike Slovenia, Scotland have been unable to find the right pass in behind the home side’s defence. Gilmour then carelessly gives the ball away as Scotland’s latest spell of possession ends.

Sources indicate that since Slovenia wasted that 14th-minute chance, Scotland have grown into the contest and are beginning to look comfortable in possession. However, they’re still waiting to craft their first notable opening here.

It has been revealed that the hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

Industry observers note that matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

Sources indicate that slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

Gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is launched forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

In a recent development, slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

The hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

Both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

On paper, it looks like Sebastien Pocognoli has opted for a five-back formation, with Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh making his Scotland debut as one of the centre backs.

Captain Andy Robertson and Brentford’s Aaron Hickey will operate as the wing-backs, with Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and John McGinn forming a midfield three.

A upcoming-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

“A good result can help but the most crucial thing is we see things that we work on through the week. I hope is we apply that well then we will get the result which will be the perfect mix.

“I hope we can bring a good game, and a good exciting principle on the pitch. I think we need the support from the supporters because there’s a lot of new players.

Recent findings suggest that “We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

Sources indicate that scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his new role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 10:35, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:37.

Francesco Pio Esposito was in sensational form on Sunday, scoring a hat-trick in Inter Milan's 4-4 draw with Atalanta BC in Serie A.

The 21-year-old has now netted seven times and registered two assists in 14 appearances for Inter during the 2026-27 campaign, and there is presently a host of speculation surrounding his future at San Siro.

Manchester United allegedly recently scouted the 6ft 3in striker, with the Red Devils planning to bring in a upcoming forward next year.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with Esposito, who has 18 goals and nine assists in 64 appearances for Inter in all competitions.

As expected, the form of the Italy international against Atalanta drew huge praise from the Italian media.

What did the Italian media say about Esposito performance?

Corriere dello Sport handed Esposito an overall performance rating of 8/10 and branded the striker "unstoppable" for his excellent display.

Tuttosport called the striker "Super Pio" and focused on his contribution to Inter's attacking display, but it was still not enough to secure his side all three points.

Tuttomercatoweb said "Esposito like Haaland" during their post-match piece, with the Inter forward being compared to Manchester City and Norway striker Erling Haaland.

Meanwhile, Sky Sport Italia gave him Inter's highest rating of 8/10.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems are expected to put Man United in the market for a upcoming striker in January, but they might have to wait until the end of the campaign to bring in a big-name player in that area of the field.

Inter are remarked to value Esposito in the region of £84m, but that could prove to be a bargain if he continues to develop throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

Esposito has scored 10 times in 15 appearances for Italy, and he seemingly has the skill set to be a huge success in the Premier League.

Man United may bring in an experienced option, most likely on loan, during the January market, before launching a big-money move for Esposito next summer, providing that they are able to hold off the threat of Premier League relegation.

‘Not enough for me’ - Ex-Premier League referee weighs in on Chelsea v Leeds United controversy

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former Premier League referee Keith Hackett would not have awarded Leeds United a penalty when Dominic Calvert-Lewin was sent to ground by Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.
  • Leeds ran out as 4-1 winners at Stamford Bridge on Saturday (November 21) in a game that had its fair share of controversial moments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Search, Trends and Live Sport Specialist.

Former Premier League referee Keith Hackett would not have awarded Leeds United a penalty when Dominic Calvert-Lewin was sent to ground by Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.

Leeds ran out as 4-1 winners at Stamford Bridge on Saturday (November 21) in a game that had its fair share of controversial moments.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Early in the second half, Martinez appeared to wrap his arms around Calvert-Lewin and drag him to the ground.

Referee Michael Oliver did not award a spot-kick to the Whites and Hackett, who officiated in England’s top flight between 1992 and 1994, would have also ignored protests.

He told Football Insider: “When I look at the law, the law talks about a careless challenge, and the result of that is no sanction, but would be a free-kick.

“So, although it might seem harsh, there are grounds for the award of a penalty kick, on the basis of the goalkeeper and the defender being careless.

“But then I switch to the fact that football's a contact sport - and these things happen. What I think is the 18th law of the game, which is rarely used now, is common sense.

It has been revealed that “I'm not going to award a penalty kick for that. I'm just going to go, ‘right, fine, carry on'. But if it's a penalty, well, that's your opinion. Mine's slightly different. I'm not giving it. Not enough for me.”.

Leeds were awarded a penalty minutes later, when Morgan Rogers was judged to have handled a Jayden Bogle shot.

Calvert-Lewin stepped up and slotted home from 12 yards, putting the Whites ahead in the game. Noah Okafor later registered his second of the afternoon to extend the lead and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow late on.

The win pushed Leeds up to sixth in the Premier League table, above Xabi Alonso’s underperforming Blues.

  • Two more for him at Barnsley suggest the 32-year-old is embracing it, which is just as well as he is likely to be asked to do a similar job at Stevenage on Tuesday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the injured Reece James and Max Lowe up against it to play again this year, Lowe has been pushed into what is basically a left wing-back role since Challinor took over, despite having scored seven goals as a forward under Henrik Pedersen.

Two more for him at Barnsley suggest the 32-year-old is embracing it, which is just as well as he is likely to be asked to do a similar job at Stevenage on Tuesday.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"You can see it as quite a negative role when you've been a central striker, but he gets into one-v-one situations, which will give him chance to show what he can do," said Challinor.

Industry observers note that "I suppose that the hard bit at the minute is we would like to defend as a four, but with Sil (Swinkels) as a left-sided centre-back, he's not as comfortable as we'd like him to be in a left-back position. That's natural.

"Jammer probably has to do a little bit more defensively than we'd like but that's something that we've got to put up with at the minute.

"That's not going to change in the short-term so we've got to make sure we improve and keep working at it.".

Minimising it is partly down to those inside of him.

"We want him as high up the pitch as possible for as long as possible," explained Challinor. "For that to be the case we need to control the ball.

"If we haven't got the ball, then we have to defend and we end up closer to our goal. If we can look after the ball better and spend more time in the opposition half, he should be in and around the opposition penalty area most of the time.

"That comes down to what we do behind the ball to make sure that's the case.".

Challinor has fielded the same XI in his two league games in charge, both won. But whereas against Plymouth Argyle his side was more often in a 3-2-4-1 which at times became a 4-2-3-1, at Barnsley the emphasis was more the other way around.

Although he picks from the same squad at Broadhall Way, the manager hinted there may be changes.

It has been revealed that "It'll be the same group," he stated. "Three younger lads didn't travel on Friday – Jarv (Jarvis Thornton), Gabe (Otegbayo), and Ernie (Weaver). Sean (Fusire)was with us.

"Do we need to freshen up a little bit? We'll look at that and see how the players recover.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:59 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.
  • The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:59 EST, 19 November 2026.

One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.

Recent findings suggest that it was reported by Bloomberg last week that a German lender, Oldenburgische Landesbank (OL), had pulled out of a deal that would have let Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras take a large upfront payment against instalments City are due to pay them for midfielder Allan Elias, signed this summer for £32million with £2m add-ons. That bank views City as a reputational and financial risk.

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Apollo was in the final stages of negotiating the loan to City Football Group (CFG) in September, when the deal collapsed after the ruling that they artificially inflated their financial position to the tune of more than £900m over nine years.

City owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan injected £100m into the club in the month after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mansour, who has only been present at one City home game since Abu Dhabi bought the club in 2008, has made no public comment on the club’s conviction, which delivers huge reputational damage to his image-conscious country.

Recent findings suggest that there are signs that football is preparing for a strong legal attack from Abu Dhabi if City lose their appeal. Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors in the event of sponsors Etihad and Etisalat suing them, it was also unveiled on Thursday. Legal indemnity will be in place for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and three other non-executive directors.

US private capital group Apollo Global Management abandoned a £1.5billion loan to Man City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

City owner Sheikh Mansou injected £100m into the club after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi.

But the refusal of credit by Apollo, which has loaned £80m to Premier League football club Nottingham Forest and has a minority stake in Championship side Wrexham, demonstrates that the capital markets think City are imperilled, with the appeal process by no means straightforward.

If an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court. But to do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

Industry observers note that financial analyst Paul Quinn wrote on The Esk website that Apollo’s problem had been with City, not Abu Dhabi itself. Three weeks ago, Apollo agreed to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. Apollo and City have not commented.

Quinn said that CFG needed the money because it was not self-funding, despite City’s financial strength. CFG’s pre-tax loss widened from £122.2m to £292.3m in the last financial year. City produced £694.1m of CFG’s £888m group revenue and ran up a £9m loss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:53.

The league phase of the Champions League continues this week as the 36 teams head into matchday five looking for the win that could prove decisive in their quest to progress through to the knockout stages.

Arsenal's showdown with Borussia Dortmund is arguably the pick of the matches, with those teams sitting at the top of the Premier League and Bundesliga tables.

Nevertheless, with all of the favourites for the competition being kept apart on this particular matchday, they will view it as an opportunity to edge closer to making the top eight.

As highlighted by Sports Mole, there are just four players serving suspensions ahead of matchday five.

Fresh off the back of a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, Manchester United make the trip to Sporting Lisbon without Matheus Cunha.

Having scored what proved to be the winner in a thrilling contest with Roma, Cunha received a second yellow card for a needless challenge during the closing stages.

Meanwhile, Man City will face Napoli at the Etihad Stadium with the visitors being unable to select defender Rafa Marin.

He was dismissed for denying a goalscoring opportunity when Porto had the chance to move 4-1 up in Portugal.

As for AEK Athens, Aboubakary Koita is unavailable for their match against Como due to the red card that he was given versus Real Madrid.

Koita was handed a red card after the final whistle for a prolonged confrontation with the officials.

Sabah defender Aden McCarthy is the fourth player to miss the MD5 for his dismissal in the 4-1 defeat to Viking FK.

He now misses the home fixture against La Liga champions Barcelona.

Although Koita and McCarthy will miss matches this week, UEFA are at the moment indicating that an extra game may be added to their suspensions in due course.

This season - propelled by the goals of Will Lankshear - they have rarely been out of the promotion conversation and moved to the top of the league with Saturday’s 2-0 win over Bristol City.

“It’s been a great year, a fun year,” said Hellberg, ahead of Tuesday night’s visit of Swansea City. “I’ve learned a lot, I’ve developed together with the players and I’m feeling that the club is in a better place and further ahead than we were a year ago.

“It’s great (to be top), but it goes quick in this business and it’s a fresh game Tuesday. We’re happy with the points tally we’ve gathered and we’ve played some great football at times, but there’s always ups and downs that you have to handle in this tough league.

Sources indicate that “And as we learnt last year, it doesn’t matter how many days you are in the top two, all that matters is the last day of the season. It’s about performances and hopefully people can see we’ve made strides forward.”.

Sources indicate that lankshear has scored 13 goals in 12 Championship starts but missed the defeat at Wrexham and the draw at Watford with a hamstring injury. He came off the bench for a 13-minute cameo at the weekend.

Hellberg confirmed on Monday he is “ready to go” against Swansea.

Industry News: Bradford City v Barnsley FC: Patrick Kelly tells Reds to stop using youth as an excuse

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whereas the Bantams’ squad is built around players who have been around the block, Barnsley's is the complete opposite.
  • Kelly, one of eight starters below the age of 23, wore the captain's armband in Friday's 2-1 defeat at Sheffield Wednesday, although 31-year-old midfielder Cameron McGeehan is almost certain to return from suspension at Valley Parade.
  • Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whereas the Bantams’ squad is built around players who have been around the block, Barnsley's is the complete opposite.

Kelly, one of eight starters below the age of 23, wore the captain's armband in Friday's 2-1 defeat at Sheffield Wednesday, although 31-year-old midfielder Cameron McGeehan is almost certain to return from suspension at Valley Parade.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The callowness of the Reds has been exposed at times this season but as part of a young Northern Ireland team which has had an exceptional start to the season, winning promotion to the top division of the Nations League, Kelly is loathe to use that as an excuse.

"The Northern Ireland team is young, but it's a really experienced team," stressed former Doncaster Rovers player Kelly. "I think if you look at the amount of caps some of the lads have, the Charles brothers (former Sheffield Wednesday players Shea and Pierce) are 23 and 21, but they've played (a combined 57) international games.

"Here it's a lot of lads' first seasons in the EFL, which is completely different.

"But I think young players are fearless and we probably do need to stop looking at us as a young team.

"I don't actually think that's the reason why we're losing so many games. It's nothing to do with that, I think.".

Whilst the age of the squad probably is a bigger factor than Kelly will admit, he is right that there is no point falling back on it as that will not change this side of the January transfer window at the very earliest.

What Barnsley’s strategy is meant to do is accelerate the development of young players, and Kelly feels wearing the captain's armband – or even taking on more responsibility when others do – is enhancing his game.

Industry observers note that "I really enjoy it," he mentioned. "It was a bit different for me coming back this season. From the very start, it was just a lot of a younger changing room.

Recent findings suggest that "I felt really older when I came back compared to when I joined here last year. But it'll be really good for me in the future. I'm quite enjoying it.

"I'm looking up to Carm a lot, the captain of the group. I speak with him nearly every day. He's really helping me.".

But the focus just has to be on securing a first win in 11 league games.

"We've got a chance to try and bounce back," said Kelly. "We need to start winning games, so hopefully start on Tuesday.

"It will be another significant crowd, with a good atmosphere.

"It just makes everyone play another five to ten per cent better, run a bit more when there's a massive crowd. I think the big atmospheres do help.

"Hopefully, it'll help us track a win on Tuesday.".

Daniel Stendel has a decision to make at right-back after Jubril Okedina – a central defender playing out of position there – was culpable for goals in the last two matches.

“It’s a little bit like our performance," mentioned the coach. "We played well but in little moments we are not ready and conceded the goal. He is similar.

According to recent reports, "It was not only his fault but he was the last player and maybe he can defend this ball better. It was team mistakes.

“We have the chance to do it better at Bradford and we have some ideas to change some things in the first 11, maybe not.”.

After four games out of the XI, Tyrese Noslin is an option.

It has been revealed that "I think a little bit in the first games it’s not his quality in possession that he has to improve, it’s more his physical game out of possession," noted Stendel. "He tried to adapt his game so much more in training every week.

"I hope maybe on Tuesday or maybe Saturday he is ready to start and show he does the next step in his career.".

Striker Tobi Adeyemo is not expected to feature again in 2026, but on-loan winger Amani Richards has an outside chance of playing before Christmas.

Leeds United manager Daniel Farke reserved praise for a trio of fringe players after the importance of squad depth was highlighted against Chelsea.

Substitutes hammered the final nail into the Chelsea coffin on Saturday (November 21), when an incisive pass from winger Harry Wilson allowed playmaker Brenden Aaronson to wrap up a 4-1 away victory.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Wilson had replaced midfielder Sean Longstaff, who has emerged from the periphery to start and play a key role in back-to-back wins.

All three were namechecked post-match by Farke, who has warmly welcomed contributions from players not considered regular starters.

He told The Yorkshire Post: “[I am] very pleased because Brenden had perhaps a period when he was not playing with this clarity in this game, and for that he had to wait a few games for his chance.

“But I have to say, I watched him carefully during this international break. He looked really sharp and much better in possession and training, with more clarity in his game.

“I had a good feeling when I brought him on, and this is why he also deserves to be in the spotlight today, because it was a well-taken goal, but also his touches before, it was more belief and more bravery and clarity than in the games before, and he has shown this in training.

“Hard work on the training pitch is always the answer. I'm a major believer in you play how you train. He has trained really well during the international break, and for that I was also confident that he could make an impact today. We need this.

“Sean Longstaff has chipped in, after he had not too many minutes in the beginning of the season, right now also really excellent performances.

“Harry Wilson today again with another key pass, also before the goal, so it's notable that he makes an impact.”.

After Leeds’ win over Tottenham Hotspur prior to the international break, Melvin Bard’s impact from the bench featured prominently in post-match discussions.

Farke’s leading lights tend to hog the headlines, yet the German is keen for every member of the squad to believe they can have an impact.

He said: “We can't compete on this level with other clubs in terms of spending money or individual quality.

Sources indicate that “We need to be competitive as a whole unit, as a whole team, and this is the unity that the players have and the belief that everyone can chip in. This is the key, and exactly in this way we want to keep going.”.

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 12:02.

Industry observers note that paris Saint-Germain have recently made enquiries about Estevao and Rayan, who are not available in the January transfer window. The capital club have a third, more accessible Brazilian talent on their radar.

Injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue could force PSG to revise their prepares for the January window. Both forwards have suffered anterior cruciate ligament ruptures and could miss the whole season. Faced with these two major absences, boss Luis Enrique and Luis Campos are studying different options to strengthen the Parisian attack.

With Eli Junior Kroupi and Paris Brunner ruled out as options, the French club have notably made enquiries about three young Brazilian talents in recent weeks, according to TeamTalk.

Sources indicate that PSG contacted Chelsea to find out the conditions of a possible transfer for Estevao. The 19-year-old winger, who arrived from Palmeiras, is highly rated by the Parisian hierarchy. His limited playing time this season had raised hopes of an opening, but Chelsea promptly ruled out that possibility.

The London club are counting on their Brazil international for the coming years and do not wish to part with him, even temporarily.

The situation is similar for Rayan. The 20-year-old winger, who plays for Bournemouth, is also on the Parisian radar. But Bournemouth are no more inclined to let their gem leave in the middle of the season.

According to the outlet, another Brazilian gem is being closely watched by the Parisian recruiters: Alisson Santana.

The 21-year-old winger currently plays for Shakhtar Donetsk and is enjoying a convincing start to the season. The Brazilian has scored six goals and provided five assists in 16 games. His performances have attracted the attention of PSG scouts.

Alisson is regarded as 'a much more accessible target' by TeamTalk. Presently valued at £11m (€13m), the recently capped Brazil international would, however, be more of a long-term signing than one for the second half of the season. His profile could also raise questions, as he is mainly used as a right winger, while versatility is very important to Luis Enrique.

Recent findings suggest that PSG have not, however, limited their search to the Brazilian market. Two other attacking profiles followed in the Bundesliga, Ibrahim Maza and Stated El Mala, who has already reacted to the PSG rumour, are also among the players liked by the Parisian recruitment team.

The recruitment team still have six weeks before the January transfer window opens.

Former England forward Mark Hateley believes consistency is key for Leeds United defender Jayden Bogle as he targets a maiden Three Lions call-up.

The 26-year-old was a £5m acquisition in the summer of 2024, when the Whites prised him from their South Yorkshire rivals Sheffield United.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has gone from strength to strength in LS11, developing into one of Daniel Farke’s most trusted lieutenants.

Bogle has made no secret of his desire to break into the England squad, but faces stiff competition from high-profile stars.

According to recent reports, “You just don't get into the England team now,” Hateley told The Yorkshire Post. “We have a lot of good players.

“You just have to look at the World Cup, some of the players that didn't go to the World Cup. We are where we are. We've got a Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane.

In a recent development, “You've probably got another two or three England players right now that could be Ballon d'Or winners in the next 5/10 years easily. That's the sort of opposition you've got trying to get into this England team. I'm not going to say team, I'm going to say squad.

“Consistency will do the young man well. I think Jayden, he's put in his performances. He's of a good age. He's not that fully developed player, but he is playing well, consistently well. You put that together over another year or another season, you're 27, 28, then who knows?”.

Bogle was capped by England at under-20 level while on the books of Derby County and featured in the 2019 Toulon Tournament.

Two of his Leeds teammates - James Trafford and Dominic Calvert-Lewin - were named in Thomas Tuchel’s last England squad.

Industry observers note that “A lot of opportunities can come your way,” remarked Hateley, who had a loan spell at Leeds in 1996. “Doors open.

“When that door does open, you have to steam into that door. You can only do that by having that consistency.”.

David Raya was not involved in Arsenal’s open training session on Monday morning.

The Spaniard was forced off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League on Saturday evening, as the Gunners dropped two points at St James’ Park.

Raya suffered what looked like a shoulder injury during a seemingly innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula.

He went down hurt and required treatment, and had to be replaced by deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya appeared to be in significant pain as he came off and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admitted after the match that it was “not good news”.

Raya was sent for scans on Sunday and while the results of those have not yet been confirmed by the club, he did not train with his team-mates on Monday morning.

Kepa and Illan Meslier went through the usual goalkeeping drills without their team-mate at London Colney.

It leaves Raya as a major doubt for Arsenal’s Champions League match at home to Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Arteta will provide an update on Raya’s injury and any potential spell on the sidelines at his pre-match press conference later on Monday.

The massive matches come thick and fast for the Gunners in the coming weeks.

Arsenal host Manchester City in the Premier League at the weekend, before making the short trip across north London to take on arch-rivals Tottenham seven days later.

There are also showdowns with both Real Madrid and Manchester United coming up before Christmas.

#163693. Latest Update: 'If you don't give him what he wants, he'll burn your house down': Inside the 'cult' of Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as sources from his crumbling sporting empire reveal the destructive know-it-all arrogance of Man United co-owner and his henchmen

Latest Update: 'If you don't give him what he wants, he'll burn your house down': Inside the 'cult' of Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as sources from his crumbling sporting empire reveal the destructive know-it-all arrogance of Man United co-owner and his henchmen

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1616 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail
